data.name: Objectives, Endpoints, and Estimands
data.text:
For definitions of the UC-specific endpoints, see Section 8.1.

Objectives Endpoints Primary To evaluate if concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) is superior to mirikizumab and placebo in simultaneously achieving clinical remission and weight reduction  Proportion of participants who simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 52 Key Secondary To evaluate the effect of treatment with concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) versus mirikizumab and placebo as measured by gastroenterologic outcomes  Proportion of participants who achieve the following at Week 52:

o clinical remission o endoscopic response o histologic-endoscopic mucosal improvement plus absence of neutrophils Additional Secondary To evaluate the effect of treatment with concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) versus mirikizumab and placebo as measured by gastroenterologic and patient-reported outcomes  Proportion of participants who achieve the following at Week 24:

o clinical remission o endoscopic response o histologic-endoscopic mucosal improvement plus absence of neutrophils  Proportion of participants who achieve the following at Week 52:

o maintenance of clinical remission o corticosteroid-free remission  Proportion of participants who achieve the following at Week 24 and Week 52:

o clinical response o endoscopic remission o Bowel Movement Urgency improvement (captured with Urgency NRS) o histologic improvement o histologic remission; that is, histologic improvement with absence of neutrophils o Bowel Urgency remission  Proportion of participants who achieve symptomatic remission at Weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, and 52  Proportion of participants who achieve symptomatic response at Weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, and 52  Proportion of participants who simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 5% weight reduction at Week 24 and Week 52  Proportion of participants who simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 24 44 Objectives Endpoints  Change from baseline in biomarkers: CRP and fecal calprotectin, at various time points (Weeks 4, 12, 24, and 52)  Change from baseline at Week 24 and Week 52 in o IBDQ o EQ-5D-5L o WPAI:UC o PGR-S  Proportion of participants at Week 52 who had o resolution of EIMs among those who had EIMs at baseline o UC-related emergency room visits o UC-related hospitalizations, and o UC-related surgeries To evaluate the effect of treatment with concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) versus mirikizumab and placebo as measured by metabolic outcomes  Proportion of participants who achieve at least a 10% reduction in body weight at Week 24 and Week 52  Percent change in body weight at Weeks 24, 40, and 52  Change in BMI (kg/m2) at Weeks 24, 40, and 52  Change in waist circumference at Weeks 8, 12, 24, 40, and 52  Change at Week 24 and Week 52 in o HbA1c (%), and o glucose (non-fasting)  Change at Week 52 in o total cholesterol (mg/dL) o TG (mg/dL) o LDL (mg/dL), and o HDL (mg/dL) (non-fasting lipids)  Change in systolic and diastolic blood pressure (mmHg) at Week 52 To describe safety and tolerability of the study interventions  TEAEs  discontinuation of study intervention due to AEs  SAEs, and  injection site reactions Exploratory Exploratory objectives and endpoints will also evaluate all the key secondary and additional secondary measures listed above at additional time points as noted in the SoA.

To demonstrate the effect of treatment with concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) versus mirikizumab and placebo as measured by efficacy and inflammatory biomarkers  Proportion of participants who achieve at least 5%, and at least 15% weight reduction at Week 24 and Week 52  Change in percentage of visceral fat mass of total body mass from baseline to Week 52a  Shift in waist-to-height ratio categories (<0.5, 0.5-0.59, ≥0.6) at Week 24 and Week 52  Changes in exploratory biomarkers To characterize the PK of mirikizumab and tirzepatide Trough serum concentrations of mirikizumab and trough plasma concentrations of tirzepatide 45 Abbreviations: AE = adverse event; CRP = C-reactive protein; BMI = body mass index; DXA = dual-energy absorptiometry; EIM = extraintestinal manifestation; HbA1c = hemoglobin A1c; HDL = high-density lipoprotein; IBDQ = Inflammatory Bowel Disease Questionnaire; LDL = low-density lipoprotein; MTD = maximum tolerated dose; NRS = numeric rating scale; PGR-S = Patient’s Global Rating of Severity; PK = pharmacokinetics; SAE = serious adverse event; SoA = schedule of activities; TEAE = treatment-emergent adverse event; TG = triglycerides; UC = ulcerative colitis; WPAI:UC = Work Productivity and Activity Impairment Questionnaire ulcerative colitis.

a Assessed via DXA scan.

Primary estimand The primary clinical question of interest is:

In participants with moderately to severely active UC who have obesity, or are overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition, what is the treatment difference between mirikizumab and placebo versus mirikizumab concomitantly administered with tirzepatide in simultaneously achieving clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 52 without early permanent discontinuation of study intervention or taking specified prohibited medication? The estimand is described by the following attributes:

 Population - Participants with moderately to severely active UC and o obesity, or o overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition:

▪ hypertension

▪ T2DM

▪ dyslipidemia

▪ obstructive sleep apnea, or

▪ cardiovascular disease.

 Endpoint – Simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 52.

 Treatment condition - Mirikizumab and placebo versus mirikizumab concomitantly administered with tirzepatide.

 ICE – Early permanent treatment discontinuation and specified prohibited medication use are addressed by the composite strategy. Participants will be considered as nonresponders after the first occurrence of these ICEs. Detailed definitions of specified prohibited medication will be provided in the SAP.

 Population-level summary - Difference in proportion of participants with response.

Rationale for estimand: The primary estimand strategy assumes the following:

 If a participant used specified prohibited medication, the participant was not receiving sufficient benefits from study intervention.

 If a participant permanently discontinued study intervention early, the participant experienced a burden of study intervention that outweighed its benefits.

Additional estimand(s) may be defined in the SAP.

46 Secondary estimand(s) The clinical questions of interest and estimand strategies for the key secondary objectives are the same as for the primary objective, except for the endpoints to be evaluated. These endpoints are as follows:

 clinical remission at Week 52  endoscopic response at Week 52, and  histologic-endoscopic mucosal improvement plus absence of neutrophils at Week 52.

Additional estimand(s) for other secondary objectives will be provided in the SAP.

data.name: Study Population
data.text:
Participant eligibility for enrollment in the study is based on the criteria listed in this section. The inclusion and exclusion criteria used to determine eligibility should only apply at screening or other specified visits, and not continuously throughout the study.

Prospective approval of protocol deviations to recruitment and enrollment criteria, also known as protocol waivers or exemptions, is not permitted.

data.name: Study Intervention(s) and Concomitant Therapy
data.text: Study intervention is defined as any medicinal product(s) or medical device(s) intended to be administered to or used by a study participant according to the study protocol.

data.text: Discontinuation/Withdrawal Discontinuation of specific sites or of the study as a whole are handled as part of Section 10.1.

data.name: Study Assessments and Procedures
data.text:
Study procedures and their timing are summarized in the SoA.

Immediate safety concerns should be discussed with the sponsor immediately upon occurrence or awareness to determine if the participant should continue or discontinue study intervention.

Adherence to the study design requirements, including those specified in the SoA, is essential and required for study conduct.

All screening evaluations must be completed and reviewed to confirm that potential participants meet all eligibility criteria. The investigator will maintain a screening log to record details of all participants screened and to confirm eligibility or record reasons for screening failure, as applicable.

data.text: The first version of SAP will be finalized prior to first unblinding, and it will include a more technical and detailed description of the statistical analyses described in this section. data.name: Synopsis
data.text:
Protocol Title: A Phase 3b, Randomized, Multicenter, Controlled Study of Mirikizumab and Placebo or Mirikizumab Concomitantly Administered with Tirzepatide in Adult Participants with Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis and Obesity or Overweight Brief Title: Mirikizumab and Tirzepatide Concomitantly Administered in Adult Participants with Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis and Obesity or Overweight: Phase 3b Study Regulatory Agency Identifier Number(s):

IND: 174802 EU trial number: 2024-520209-38-00 Rationale:

Over 50% of patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) have obesity or overweight. Obesity in patients with UC is independently associated with higher burden and costs of hospitalizations. Bariatric surgery has been shown to result in lower use of medication for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and improved IBD outcomes.

This study, I6T-MC-AMCD (AMCD), aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mirikizumab and placebo compared with mirikizumab and concomitantly administered tirzepatide in adult participants with moderately to severely active UC and obesity, or overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition, including  hypertension  type 2 diabetes mellitus  dyslipidemia  obstructive sleep apnea, or  cardiovascular disease.

Objectives, Endpoints, and Estimands:

Objectives Endpoints Primary To evaluate if concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) is superior to mirikizumab and placebo in simultaneously achieving clinical remission and weight reduction  Proportion of participants who simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 52 Key Secondary To evaluate the effect of treatment with concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) versus mirikizumab and placebo as measured by gastroenterologic outcomes  Proportion of participants who achieve the following at Week 52:

o clinical remission o endoscopic response 11 Objectives Endpoints o histologic-endoscopic mucosal improvement plus absence of neutrophils Additional Secondary To evaluate the effect of treatment with concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) versus mirikizumab and placebo as measured by gastroenterologic and patient-reported outcomes  Proportion of participants who achieve the following at Week 24:

o clinical remission o endoscopic response o histologic-endoscopic mucosal improvement plus absence of neutrophils  Proportion of participants who achieve the following at Week 52:

o maintenance of clinical remission o corticosteroid-free remission  Proportion of participants who achieve the following at Week 24 and Week 52:

o clinical response o endoscopic remission o Bowel Movement Urgency improvement (captured with Urgency NRS) o histologic improvement o histologic remission; that is, histologic improvement with absence of neutrophils o Bowel Urgency remission  Proportion of participants who achieve symptomatic remission at Weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, and 52  Proportion of participants who achieve symptomatic response at Weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, and 52  Proportion of participants who simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 5% weight reduction at Week 24 and Week 52  Proportion of participants who simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 24  Change from baseline in biomarkers: CRP and fecal calprotectin, at various time points (Weeks 4, 12, 24, and 52)  Change from baseline at Week 24 and Week 52 in o IBDQ o EQ-5D-5L o WPAI:UC o PGR-S  Proportion of participants at Week 52 who had o resolution of EIMs among those who had EIMs at baseline o UC-related emergency room visits o UC-related hospitalizations, and o UC-related surgeries To evaluate the effect of treatment with concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the  Proportion of participants who achieve at least a 10% reduction in body at Week 24 and Week 52 12 Objectives Endpoints MTD (up to 15 mg) versus mirikizumab and placebo as measured by metabolic outcomes  Percent change in body weight at Weeks 24, 40, and 52  Change in BMI (kg/m2) at Weeks 24, 40, and 52  Change in waist circumference at Weeks 8, 12, 24, 40, and 52  Change at Week 24 and Week 52 in o HbA1c (%), and o glucose (non-fasting)  Change at Week 52 in o total cholesterol (mg/dL) o TG (mg/dL) o LDL (mg/dL), and o HDL (mg/dL) (non-fasting lipids)  Change in systolic and diastolic blood pressure (mmHg) at Week 52 To describe safety and tolerability of the study interventions  TEAEs  discontinuation of study intervention due to AEs  SAEs, and  injection site reactions Abbreviations: AE = adverse event; CRP = C-reactive protein; BMI = body mass index; EIM = extraintestinal manifestation; HbA1c = hemoglobin A1c; HDL = high-density lipoprotein; IBDQ = Inflammatory Bowel Disease Questionnaire; LDL = low-density lipoprotein; MTD = maximum tolerated dose; NRS = numeric rating scale; PGR-S = Patient’s Global Rating of Severity; SAE = serious adverse event; TEAE = treatment-emergent adverse event; TG = triglycerides; UC = ulcerative colitis; WPAI:UC = Work Productivity and Activity Impairment Questionnaire ulcerative colitis.

The primary clinical question of interest is:

In participants with moderately to severely active UC who have obesity, or are overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition, what is the treatment difference between mirikizumab and placebo versus mirikizumab concomitantly administered with tirzepatide in simultaneously achieving clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 52 without early permanent discontinuation of study intervention or taking specified prohibited medication? Overall Design:

Study AMCD is a Phase 3b, randomized, multicenter study to assess the efficacy and safety of mirikizumab and placebo compared with mirikizumab concomitantly administered with tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) in adult participants with moderately to severely active UC and obesity, or overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition.

The maximum duration of this study is approximately 61 weeks, with the following study periods:

 Study Period I, Screening: up to 5 weeks (≤35 days)  Study Period II, Induction and Dose Escalation: 24 weeks  Study Period III, Maintenance Treatment: 28 weeks, and  Safety follow-up: 4 weeks after the last visit.

Brief Summary:

13 The participants in this study will have UC and obesity, or overweight in the presence of at least 1 weight-related illness at the same time.

The main purpose of this study is to show whether in these individuals, treatment with both mirikizumab and tirzepatide, compared with treatment with mirikizumab and placebo, leads to  decrease or disappearance of UC symptoms, and  loss of at least one-tenth of the overall body weight.

Study details include:

 The study duration will be up to 61 weeks.

 The treatment duration will be up to 52 weeks.

 The visit frequency will be every 4 weeks during the treatment period. Between Week 28 and Week 48, some of the visits will be conducted by telephone.

Study Population:

In general, an individual may participate in this study if they  Are ≥18 to ≤70 years of age.

 Have had an established diagnosis of UC for ≥3 months before Visit 2, which includes endoscopic evidence of UC and a histopathology report that supports a diagnosis of UC.

 Have o obesity (body mass index ≥30 kg/m2), or o overweight (body mass index ≥27 kg/m2 to <30 kg/m

2) and in the presence of at least 1 of these weight-related comorbid conditions:

▪ hypertension

▪ type 2 diabetes mellitus

▪ dyslipidemia

▪ obstructive sleep apnea, or

▪ cardiovascular disease.

 Have moderately to severely active UC as defined by an mMS of 5 to 9 points and Endoscopic Subscore of 2 to 3 (confirmed by central review) within 21 days before Visit 2.

In general, an individual may not take part in the study if they  Have a current diagnosis of o Crohn’s disease o IBD unclassified (formerly known as indeterminate colitis), or o primary sclerosing cholangitis.

 Have a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes or have insulin-treated type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Number of Participants:

Approximately 350 participants will be randomly assigned to mirikizumab and placebo or mirikizumab and tirzepatide used concomitantly, in a 1:1 randomization ratio.

14 The randomly assigned study population will include up to approximately 70% of either individuals assigned female at birth or assigned male at birth, whoever enrolls faster. The remaining sex will make up the remainder of the participant population.

Intervention Groups and Duration:

This table lists the interventions used in this study:

Intervention Name Mirikizumab Tirzepatide Placebo to match tirzepatide Study Treatment Induction Maintenance Dosage Level(s) 300 mg at Weeks 0, 4, and 8 200 mg Q4W starting at Week 12, given as 2 consecutive injections of 100 mg each All doses QW:

 2.5 mg  5 mg  7.5 mg  10 mg  12.5 mg  15 mg QW Route of Administration IV infusion SC (prefilled syringe) Administration Onsite:

 only by authorized study personnel  maximum rate of 10 mg/min by IV infusion over no less than 30 min Initial administration:

 Onsite, either o as self-administration by participant or caregiver, after appropriate training and under supervision of study personnel, or o by study personnel.

Subsequent administration:

 offsite (for example, at participant’s home) by the participant or their caretaker after completion of training, or  onsite, by authorized study personnel (per participant’s preference).

Authorized as defined by EU Clinical Trial Regulation Authorized and not used according to EU authorizationa Authorized and not used according to EU authorizationb Not authorized in EU Abbreviations: EU = European Union; IV = intravenous; Q4W = every 4 weeks; QW = every week; SC = subcutaneous; T2DM = type 2 diabetes mellitus; UC = ulcerative colitis.

a Mirikizumab is authorized in EU for the treatment of UC. In this study, clinical trial material will be used for mirikizumab.

b Tirzepatide is authorized in EU for the treatment of T2DM and for weight management, including weight loss and weight maintenance, in patients with obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbid condition. In this study, clinical trial material will be used for tirzepatide.

Ethical Considerations of Benefit/Risk:

Taking into account the measures taken to minimize risk to participants participating in this study, the potential risks identified in association with mirikizumab and placebo or mirikizumab concomitantly administered with tirzepatide are justified by the anticipated benefits that may be afforded to participants with UC with obesity, or overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition.

data.name: Study Rationale
data.text:
Over 50% of patients with UC have obesity or overweight. Obesity in patients with UC is independently associated with higher burden and costs of hospitalizations. Bariatric surgery has been shown to result in lower use of medication for IBD and improved IBD outcomes.

This study, I6T-MC-AMCD (AMCD), aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mirikizumab and placebo compared with mirikizumab and concomitantly administered tirzepatide in adult participants with moderately to severely active UC and obesity, or overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition, including  hypertension  T2DM  dyslipidemia  obstructive sleep apnea, or  cardiovascular disease.

Mirikizumab was first approved in Japan on 27 March 2023. Mirikizumab has been approved in multiple geographies for the treatment of moderately to severely active UC in patients 18 years of age and above (Omvoh™ package insert, 2024; Omvoh summary of product characteristics).

Tirzepatide is approved as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition, in the United States and EU, with applications either approved or under review in other regions (Zepbound® package insert, 2024; Mounjaro® summary of product characteristics).

data.name: Background
data.text:
Mirikizumab Mirikizumab is a humanized IgG4-variant monoclonal antibody that binds to the p19 subunit of IL-23 without binding to other members of the IL-12 cytokine family. Mirikizumab is being developed for the treatment of immune-mediated diseases in which the IL-23 pathway is thought to have a pathogenic role.

Mirikizumab Phase 3 induction Study I6T-MC-AMAN (AMAN) and maintenance Study I6T- MC-AMBG (AMBG) results demonstrated the consistent and robust efficacy of mirikizumab in the treatment of moderately to severely active UC.

Tirzepatide Tirzepatide is a GIP receptor and GLP-1 receptor agonist. Tirzepatide is indicated as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition (Zepbound package insert, 2024; Mounjaro summary of product characteristics).

38 Unmet medical need Approximately 55.4% of patients with UC have obesity or overweight (Newberry and Lichtenstein 2013; Johnson et al. 2021).

Obesity leads to more rapid clearance and lower trough concentrations of biologic agents in patients with IBD and is associated with decreased treatment responsiveness to biologics (Bassi and Singh 2022). In the mirikizumab UC Phase 3 Study AMAN, for clinical remission and endoscopic response, there was a numerical trend for participants with obesity to have reduced response to mirikizumab compared with participants who had a normal weight. This numerical trend was unrelated to mirikizumab exposure.

In addition, obesity in patients with IBD, including UC, is independently associated with higher burden and costs of hospitalizations (Nguyen et al. 2019; El-Dallal et al. 2021). Similarly, bariatric surgery has been shown to be safe in patients with IBD and results in lower use of medication for IBD and improved IBD outcomes (Wise et al. 2022).

GLP-1 and inflammation GLP-1 is involved in modulating inflammation by inhibiting mucosal cytokines and gut epithelial architecture in animal models of colitis, leading to mucosal healing suggesting that GLP-1 analogs may have an anti-inflammatory effect in patients with IBD colitis (Anbazhagan et al. 2017).

GLP-1 receptor agonists and IBD A Danish registry of patients with IBD and T2DM showed that there was a decreased risk of IBD-related hospitalization and IBD-related surgery among users of GLP-1-based therapies compared with non-GLP-1-based therapies (Villumsen et al. 2021).

Alchirazi et al. (2024) conducted a US cohort propensity-matched study with over 14,000 patients with IBD, which included both CD and UC cohorts. In patients with UC, comparing patients who did or did not receive GLP-1 receptor agonists, those who did were less likely to  be hospitalized  undergo colectomy  require steroids, or  have colon cancer.

In a recent study, patients withT2DM in an Israeli nationwide cohort of patients with IBD and GLP-1 analog exposure for at least 6 months had improved outcomes in IBD, specifically in patients with obesity (Gorelik et al. 2024).

In a population-based cohort study in 10,855 adult patients using administrative health data from British Columbia, patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases such as IBD and T2DM taking GLP-1 receptor agonists had fewer major adverse cardiovascular events and a lower chance of death compared with those taking DPP-4 inhibitors (Karacabeyli et al. 2024).

Among an IBD cohort comprised of patients with diabetes and patients without diabetes, GLP-1 receptor agonists were well tolerated and were not associated with major adverse IBD outcomes.

Additionally, GLP-1 receptor agonists were effective and associated with significant decreases in BMI and hemoglobin A1c. These changes were not significantly different from those observed in 39 a control group without IBD who initiated a GLP-1 receptor agonist during the same time. The study’s findings therefore suggest that GLP-1 receptor agonists can be comfortably prescribed for patients with IBD (Levine et al. 2024).

data.name: Benefit/Risk Assessment
data.text:
Detailed information about the known and expected benefits and risks and reasonably expected AEs of mirikizumab and tirzepatide may be found in the relevant IBs and prescribing information.

2.3.1.

Risk Assessment 2.3.1.1.

Study Interventions Mirikizumab Evaluation of safety data from mirikizumab clinical studies examining psoriasis, UC, and CD shows a safety profile consistent with the anti-IL-23p19 antibody class. The risks (adverse drug reactions) found to be associated with mirikizumab include  injection site reactions  infusion-related hypersensitivity reactions  upper respiratory tract infections  ALT and AST increases  headache, and  rash.

In addition, the following special warnings and precautions for use are recommended when using mirikizumab:

 Serious hypersensitivity reactions: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, may occur with mirikizumab administration. If a serious hypersensitivity reaction occurs, discontinue mirikizumab immediately and initiate appropriate therapy.

 Infections: Mirikizumab may increase the risk of infection. Treatment with mirikizumab should not be initiated in patients with a clinically important active infection until the infection resolves or is adequately treated. Consider the risks and benefits of treatment prior to initiating the use of mirikizumab in patients with a chronic infection or a history of recurrent infection. Instruct patients to seek medical advice if signs or symptoms of clinically important acute or chronic infection occur. If a serious infection develops, consider discontinuation of mirikizumab until the infection resolves. Mirikizumab should not be given to patients with active TB. Consider anti-TB therapy before starting mirikizumab in patients with latent TB.

 Hepatic enzyme elevations: Elevations of aminotransferases have been reported in patients receiving mirikizumab. Evaluate liver enzymes as clinically indicated. If 40 increases in ALT or AST are observed and drug-associated liver injury is suspected, discontinue mirikizumab until this diagnosis is excluded (Section 8.2.9).

 Immunizations: Avoid the use of live vaccines in patients treated with mirikizumab. No data are available on the response to live or non-live vaccines.

Tirzepatide Tirzepatide has not been studied in patients with severe GI disease.

Gastrointestinal adverse reactions Tirzepatide has been associated with GI adverse reactions, sometimes severe, which include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. These adverse reactions may lead to dehydration, which could lead to a deterioration in renal function, including acute renal failure. Patients treated with tirzepatide should be advised of the potential risk of dehydration, due to the GI adverse reactions and take precautions to avoid fluid depletion and electrolyte disturbances. This should particularly be considered in the elderly, who may be more susceptible to such complications.

Potential malnutrition Events related to malnutrition have been reported, including severe, in patients receiving tirzepatide. Risks associated with malnutrition include, but are not limited to, vitamin and mineral deficiency, protein deficiency, and low body weight.

Gallbladder disease Gallbladder problems including gallstones have been reported uncommonly in patients taking tirzepatide and GLP-1 receptor agonists. In the tirzepatide SURMOUNT trials, cholelithiasis was reported in 1.1%, cholecystitis was reported in 0.7%, and cholecystectomy was reported in 0.2% of tirzepatide-treated patients. Risk may be increased if patients have diabetes or obesity and in cases of rapid weight loss. Some gallbladder problems may need surgery.

Potential risk of aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation An increasing safety concern has emerged regarding the use of GLP-1 receptor agonists in the perioperative setting, particularly due to the risk of delayed gastric emptying and subsequent aspiration during endoscopic and surgical procedures. Reports indicate instances of pulmonary aspiration of gastric contents in patients on GLP-1 receptor agonists undergoing sedation or general anesthesia, prompting a multi-society clinical practice guidance published on 29 October 2024, by various medical organizations including the American Gastroenterological Association and the American Society of Anesthesiologists (Kindel et al. 2024). It is recommended that investigators follow their local guidelines about GLP-1 agonists and deep sedation. Adhering to these recommendations can enhance patient safety during endoscopic and surgical procedures (Kindel et al. 2024). See Section 10.15 for recommendations for the safe use of GLP-1 receptor agonists during anesthesia or deep sedation, per the multisociety clinical practice guidance (Kindel et al. 2024).

Concomitant use of mirikizumab and tirzepatide There are no contraindications per approved labeling for the use of both medications concomitantly. This Phase 3b study will use the marketed dosing regimens per prescribing information for mirikizumab and tirzepatide to evaluate the relative benefit/risk profile 41 associated with concomitant use of mirikizumab and tirzepatide in participants with UC with obesity or overweight.

Drug-drug interactions There is accumulated safety data individually for mirikizumab and tirzepatide (see IBs). The concern for drug-drug interactions (anti-IL-23-p19 antibody with a small molecule like tirzepatide) is thought to be minimal but has not been assessed clinically. Tirzepatide is not considered immunosuppressive.

2.3.1.2.

Study Procedures Risks due to Common Study Procedures in Study AMCD Potential Risks of Clinical Significance Summary of Data/ Rationale for Risk Mitigation Strategy Risk associated with the endoscopic procedures Potential risk of aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation These risks are considered rare but are recognized by the US and EU labelling information (Zepbound package insert; Mounjaro, summary of product characteristics).

See “Potential risk of aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation” above and Section 10.15.

Bleeding and colonic perforation These risks are considered rare but are recognized risks for endoscopic procedures (Rabeneck et

al. 2008; Arora et al.

2009).

Trained and experienced endoscopists will be performing endoscopic assessments.

2.3.1.3.

Management of Risks The potential risks will be proactively monitored. Sections 5.1, 5.2, 7.1, 8.2, and 8.3 address known potential risks associated with mirikizumab and tirzepatide or the study procedures.

2.3.2.

Benefit Assessment Mirikizumab Mirikizumab is approved for the treatment of moderately to severely active UC (Section 2.1). At the time of this benefit/risk assessment, mirikizumab has demonstrated efficacy in Phase 2 and Phase 3 placebo-controlled studies in adults with  psoriasis (Reich et al. 2019; Papp et al. 2020)  UC (Sandborn et al. 2018; D’Haens et al. 2019, 2022), and  CD (Sands et al. 2022; Ferrante et al. 2024).

In the Phase 3 Studies AMAN and AMBG, over periods of 12 weeks and 40 weeks respectively, mirikizumab therapy had efficacy in both induction and maintenance phases across clinical, 42 symptomatic, endoscopic, and histologic measures of disease, even after treatment failure with conventional immunosuppressive agents, biologic therapies, or tofacitinib.

Participants in Study AMCD have obesity or are overweight. The prevalence of NASH in patients with morbid obesity has been reported to be 37% (Machado et al. 2006). Those with NASH, especially in the presence of fibrosis, are at a higher risk for adverse outcomes, including overall mortality, liver transplantation, or liver-related events (Angulo et al. 2015). The beneficial effects of weight loss in patients with NASH/MASH are well characterized (Promrat et al. 2010; Vilar-Gomez et al. 2015; Loomba et al. 2024). Treatment with tirzepatide results in glucose lowering, weight loss, and improved metabolic health in patients with T2DM (Frias et al.

2018).

Tirzepatide SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-2 trials demonstrated the superiority of tirzepatide to placebo as an adjunct to life intervention in achieving body weight reduction and improving cardiometabolic measures (Zepbound package insert, 2024). Weight reduction in “tirzepatide-treated” participants started to differ from those in placebo as early as Week 4. The rate of weight reduction was higher in the first 24 weeks in tirzepatide-treated participants, with most of the weight reduction (approximately 12 to 17% of baseline weight) achieved at Week 36, as compared with 3% in those on placebo (Jastreboff et al. 2022). The weight reduction continued until the study was completed at Week 72.

2.3.3.

Overall Benefit Risk Conclusion Taking into account the measures taken to minimize risk to participants in this study, the potential risks identified in association with mirikizumab and placebo or mirikizumab concomitantly administered with tirzepatide are justified by the anticipated benefits that may be afforded to participants with UC with obesity, or overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition.

43

data.name: Overall Design
data.text:
Study AMCD is a Phase 3b, randomized, multicenter study to assess the efficacy and safety of mirikizumab and placebo compared with mirikizumab concomitantly administered with tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) in adult participants with moderately to severely active UC and obesity, or overweight and in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition.

The maximum duration of this study is approximately 61 weeks, with the following study periods:

 Study Period I, Screening: up to 5 weeks (≤35 days)  Study Period II, Induction and Dose Escalation: 24 weeks  Study Period III, Maintenance Treatment: 28 weeks, and  Safety follow-up: 4 weeks after the last visit.

For randomization ratios and stratification factors, see Section 6.3.

data.name: Scientific Rationale for Study Design
data.text:
Study rationale Concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide in patients with UC with obesity or overweight is expected to improve gastroenterologic and/or metabolic outcomes compared with treatment with mirikizumab and placebo.

Sample size Approximately 350 participants who meet entry criteria will be randomly assigned at Visit 2 in a 1:1 ratio to either the  mirikizumab and placebo treatment arm, or  mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) concomitant administration treatment arm.

Refer to Section 9.5 for the rationale for the sample size.

Choice of primary endpoint The multi-component primary endpoint at Week 52 includes clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction.

Clinical remission Clinical remission, as defined in Section 8.1, was chosen based on regulatory guidance from FDA (2016) and EMA (2018). Both recommend a composite endpoint for both symptomatic and endoscopic remission.

At least 10% weight reduction A body weight reduction of at least 5% is considered the threshold for clinically meaningful effect on the basis of improvement in metabolic health. Greater weight reductions yield additional clinical benefits and may be required for improvement in certain weight-related 48 complications (Garvey et al. 2016) and are often more desired therapeutic goals in clinical practice.

Weight reduction of at least 10% was chosen based on SURMOUNT-1 data that all 3 doses of tirzepatide (5, 10, and 15 mg) had significantly higher percentages of participants achieving at least 10% weight reduction targets compared to placebo. Over 90% of the participants receiving 15 mg achieved at least 5% weight reduction at 72 weeks (Jastreboff et al. 2022).

Blinding Mirikizumab will be open label, tirzepatide and placebo to match will be blinded.

Data monitoring committee (DMC) See Section 10.1.5.1.

Rationale for collection of race and ethnicity data In this study, collection of demographic information includes race and ethnicity. The scientific rationale is based on the need to assess variable response in safety and/or efficacy based on race or ethnicity. This question can be answered only if all the relevant data are collected.

Race and ethnicity will be collected using a standardized self-reporting process. Participants will be asked to identify their own race and ethnicity. The process will use a 2-step procedure:

1. Ethnicity: “Hispanic or Latino,” “Not Hispanic or Latino,” and “Not Reported.”

2. Race: Permitted categories include American Indian or Alaskan Native, Asian, Black or African American, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, White, or Not Reported.

Justification for use of placebo The AMCD study design ensures that all participants receive an appropriate standard of care for UC. All participants will receive mirikizumab, which is increasingly becoming a standard of care for UC. Furthermore, all participants will receive lifestyle coaching, including dietary and exercise advice, which will lead to weight reduction in participants who are obese or overweight in both arms of the study.

Participants in the control arm receiving a placebo are not receiving placebo alone, but rather receiving a placebo in addition to standard-of-care treatment. The inclusion of a placebo in the trial is scientifically and methodologically justified to isolate the effects of tirzepatide when combined with mirikizumab. This approach ensures that any observed differences between the 2 groups can be attributed solely to tirzepatide, thereby allowing a rigorous evaluation of its efficacy and safety when used concomitantly with mirikizumab in UC. The use of a placebo does not compromise safety in participants who are overweight and obese.

4.2.1.

Patient Input into Design Efforts to reduce participant burden include  allowing telephone visits  focused clinician and participant measures at key time points, and  laboratory monitoring that is consistent with standard of care for participants with moderately to severely active UC.

49 Site identification included evaluation of diversity by geography and investigator sites.

data.name: Justification for Dose
data.text:
4.3.1.

Mirikizumab Mirikizumab will be dosed per approved product labeling. Detailed information about the efficacy, safety, and dosing rationale for mirikizumab may be found in the IB and prescribing information.

The induction and maintenance dose levels and regimens in Study AMCD were based on analyses of PK, safety, and efficacy data from the following studies of mirikizumab in participants with moderately to severely active UC (D’Haens et al. 2023):

 Study I6T-MC-AMAC: Phase 2 study with a 12-week IV induction and ≤92-week SC maintenance  Study AMAN (LUCENT-1): Phase 3 induction study with a 12-week IV treatment duration o Active dosing regimen: 300 mg mirikizumab IV at Weeks 0, 4, and 8, and  Study AMBG (LUCENT-2): Phase 3 maintenance study with a 40-week SC treatment duration.

o Active dosing regimen: 200 mg mirikizumab SC Q4W.

4.3.2.

Tirzepatide Tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) administered SC QW per prescribing information will be evaluated in this study. Participants may be treated with a lower maintenance dose of 5 mg or 10 mg if they do not achieve full dose-escalation to 15 mg and/or do not tolerate 15 mg.

Tirzepatide has been associated with GI adverse reactions, which include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. In general, these events were mild or moderate in severity and transient, with few severe episodes.

Dosing algorithms starting at a low dose of 2.5 mg QW accompanied by dose-escalation of 2.5-mg increments Q4W should permit time for development of tolerance to GI events and are predicted to minimize GI tolerability concerns.

Tirzepatide doses of 5 mg, 10 mg, and 15 mg as MTD are included in the prescribing information, and were selected based principally on the following criteria:

 each dose provides robust weight reduction relative to placebo  the percent of participants achieving ≥10% weight reduction is higher with 15 mg than 10 mg or 5 mg, and  safety and tolerability were supported by Phase 3 results in T2DM and obesity or overweight with weight-related comorbidity or in participants without diabetes mellitus.

The proposed tirzepatide maintenance dose of up to 15 mg using a dose-escalation regimen is expected to safely maximize the potential for weight reduction while minimizing GI tolerability concerns as has been achieved for approved GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs. The subsequent benefit of weight reduction should result in clinically meaningful improvements in participants with UC.

data.text:
The end of the study is defined as the date of the last visit of the last participant in the study or last scheduled procedure shown in the SoA for the last participant in the trial.

A participant is considered to have completed the study if the participant has completed all periods of the study, including the last visit or the last scheduled procedure shown in the SoA.

data.name: Inclusion Criteria
data.text:
Participants are eligible to be included in the study only if all of the following criteria apply:

Age

1. Must be ≥18 to ≤70 years of age at the time of signing the ICF.

Type of participant and disease characteristics

2. Have had an established diagnosis of UC for ≥3 months before baseline (Visit 2/randomization), which includes endoscopic evidence of UC and a histopathology report that supports a diagnosis of UC.

3. Have moderately to severely active UC as defined by an mMS of 5 to 9 points and ES of 2 to 3 (confirmed by central review) within 21 days before baseline.

Notes: Participants with proctitis at baseline (Visit 2) may participate in the study if they meet all the eligibility criteria for the study, including endoscopic and rectal bleeding criteria for moderate-to-severe disease. The number of such participants will be capped at 15% of the total number of participants enrolled in the study.

4. Are up-to date on colorectal cancer surveillance per local guidelines in case of  a family history of colorectal cancer  personal history of increased colorectal cancer risk  age >45 years,  history of UC for greater than or equal to 8 years or  other known risk factors.

5. Participants with a history of UC for greater than or equal to 8 years who have had a surveillance colonoscopy completed within 1 year prior to baseline must have documented negative results for colorectal dysplasia and cancer.

Note: Acceptable methods of colonoscopic surveillance include  standard-definition colonoscopy with 4 quadrant colon biopsies every 10 cm  high-definition white-light colonoscopy with narrow-band imaging and targeted colon biopsies, and  chromoendoscopy with methylene blue or indigo carmine dye spray and targeted colon biopsies.

Investigators may perform surveillance colonoscopy as part of the screening colonoscopy if they choose to do so.

6. Are willing to consult with a dietitian or nutritionist, or equivalent qualified designee or delegate* according to local standards, to receive lifestyle management counseling during 52 trial. (*Dietary counseling will be performed by a registered dietitian or nutritionist or equivalent qualified designee or delegate trained in collecting and assessing dietary intake and providing individualized dietary counseling according to the local standard).

Weight

7. Have  [7a] obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2), or  [7b] overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2 to <30 kg/m

2) and in the presence of at least 1 of these weight-related comorbid conditions:

o hypertension o T2DM o dyslipidemia o obstructive sleep apnea, or o cardiovascular disease.

Sex assigned at birth and contraceptive/barrier requirements

8. Individuals AMAB and AFAB may participate in this trial, including both IOCBP and INOCBP.

Contraceptive use by participants should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies. For the contraception requirements of this protocol, see Section 10.4.

Informed consent

9. Are capable of giving signed informed consent as described in Section 10.1, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICF and in this protocol.

Prior medication failure

10. Have an inadequate response to, loss of response to, or intolerance to at least 1 of the medications described in inclusion criterion [10a] or [10b]. Documentation of dose, frequency, route of administration, and duration of the prior failed treatment is required or could be reported by the participant.

[10a] Conventional-failed participants: Participants who  have had an inadequate response to or a loss of response to, or are intolerant to at least 1 of the following medications:

o oral corticosteroids o oral AZA or 6-MP, or o oral aminosalicylates (for example, mesalamine, sulfasalazine, olsalazine, and balsalazide) AND 53  have neither failed nor demonstrated an intolerance to an advanced therapy indicated for the treatment of UC, for example, a biologic or biosimilar medication, such as anti-TNF, anti-integrin antibody, or a JAK inhibitor.

[10b] Advanced therapy-failed participants: Participants who have an inadequate response to or a loss of response to, or are intolerant to advanced therapy for UC, defined as:

 a biologic or biosimilar medication such as anti-TNF antibodies  anti-integrin antibodies  JAK inhibitors such as tofacitinib or upadacitinib  sphingosine 1-phosphate receptor 1inhibitors such as etrasimod or ozanimod, or  anti-IL-12p40 antibodies, for example, ustekinumab.

Investigators must be able to document an adequate clinical trial of the medication if available or could be provided by patient reported history.

Notes:

 Participants previously exposed to advanced therapy who do not meet criterion [10b] must still meet criterion [10a].

 Participants previously exposed to investigational therapies for the treatment of UC must still meet criterion [10a] OR [10b].

 Participants who meet both criteria [10a] and [10b] will be considered to be “advanced therapy‑failed” for the purpose of this study.

 Oral methotrexate use will be allowed during the study; however, prior or current use of oral methotrexate is insufficient for inclusion into the study.

Ulcerative colitis medication dose stabilization

11. Are on a stable dose, defined as listed here, if using these medications:

Medication Comment  Oral 5-ASAs for UC The prescribed dose has been stable for at least 2 weeks prior to the screening colonoscopy.

 Oral corticosteroids for UC:

o prednisone ≤20 mg per day or equivalent o budesonide extended-release tablets up to 9 mg per day (budesonide MMX), or o beclomethasone dipropionate (gastro‑resistant prolonged-release tablet) up to 5 mg per day Participants on oral corticosteroids need to have been on corticosteroids for at least 4 weeks prior to screening but the prescribed dose must be stable for at least 2 weeks before the screening colonoscopy. See Section 6.9.5 for instructions on tapering of oral corticosteroid therapy.

 AZA  6-MP, or  methotrexate The prescribed dose has been stable for at least 8 weeks before the screening colonoscopy.

Diagnostic assessments

12. Have clinically acceptable central laboratory test results at screening (retesting is allowed for hematology and chemistry), as assessed by the investigator, including [12a] Hematology absolute neutrophil count ≥1.2 x 109/L (≥1.2 x 103/μL or ≥1.2 GI/L) platelet count ≥100 x 109/L (≥100 x 103/μL or ≥100 GI/L) 54 hemoglobin ≥8.5 g/dL (≥85 g/L) for individuals AMAB and >8.0 g/dL (>80 g/L) for individuals AFAB lymphocyte count ≥750 cells/μL (>0.75 x 103/μL or >0.75 GI/L) total WBC ≥2.5 x 109/L (≥2.5 x 103/μL or ≥2.5 GI/L) [12b] Chemistry serum creatinine ≤2 times ULN TBL ≤1.5 times ULN ALT and AST ≤2 times ULN ALP ≤1.5 times ULN [12c] estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2 calculated by Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) Cystatin C Equation 2012 (NKF [WWW]) [12d] calcitonin ≤35 ng/L (≤35 pg/mL) Note: Participants with an established diagnosis of Gilbert’s syndrome can be included with bilirubin levels ≤3 times ULN. The Gilbert’s syndrome diagnosis requires source documentation showing unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with no evidence of hemolysis.

Other inclusion criteria

13. Are reliable and willing to make themselves available for the duration of the study and are willing to follow study procedures as required, including, but not limited to  colonoscopies  self-injecting intervention or injection by a caregiver, when applicable  maintaining a diary  completing patient-reported questionnaires, and  storing and taking provided study interventions as directed.

data.name: Exclusion Criteria
data.text:
Participants are excluded from the study if any of the following criteria apply:

Gastrointestinal medical conditions

14. Have a current diagnosis of  Crohn’s disease  IBD unclassified (formerly known as indeterminate colitis), or  primary sclerosing cholangitis.

15. Have had or will need bowel resection or intestinal or intra-abdominal surgery, including but not limited to  extensive colonic surgery for UC, for example, subtotal colectomy, ostomy, or ileoanal pouch  any small bowel or colonic surgery within 6 months prior to baseline (Visit 2), or  any non-intestinal intra-abdominal surgery within 3 months of baseline.

16. Are likely to require surgery for the treatment of UC during the study.

Note: Participants who have had limited surgery for UC, for example, segmental colonic resection, may be allowed in the study, if this does not affect the assessment of efficacy.

Discussion with the sponsor should occur prior to screening of such participants.

55

17. Have evidence of toxic megacolon or stricture or stenosis within the colon that cannot be traversed by a sigmoidoscope or colonoscope.

Adenoma, dysplasia, or gastrointestinal cancer

18. Have any history or current evidence of cancer of the GI tract.

19. Have had prior or current GI dysplasia, other than a completely removed low-grade dysplastic lesion, before the screening endoscopy.

20. Have any adenomatous polyp without dysplasia occurring in areas of the colon and rectum, that has not been removed.

Note: If the polyp(s) has been completely removed, this criterion would no longer apply.

21. Have a diagnosis of any of the following at screening or during the study:

 cancer other than squamous cell or basal cell carcinoma of the skin (for details, see exclusion criterion [32])  any colonic adenomatous polyp with low-grade dysplasia not completely removed  any adenomatous polyp with high-grade dysplasia, or  evidence of dysplasia in nonpolypoid mucosa (indefinite for dysplasia, low-grade or high-grade dysplasia) in the GI tract.

Other medical conditions

22. Have a diagnosis of T1DM or insulin-treated T2DM.

23. Have any current or past history, or a diagnosis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, diabetic maculopathy, or nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy that requires acute treatment.

24. Have a history of severe hypoglycemia and/or hypoglycemia unawareness within the 6 months prior to Visit 1 (screening).

25. Have a history of ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar state or coma in the last year.

26. Have a self-reported change in body weight greater than 5% (gain or reduction) within 3 months prior to Visit 1.

27. Have a prior or planned surgical treatment for obesity, such as gastric bypass (bariatric) surgery or restrictive bariatric surgery (for example, Lap-Band®), excluding liposuction or abdominoplasty if performed more than 1 year prior to Visit 1.

28. Have a known clinically significant gastric emptying abnormality (for example, severe gastroparesis or gastric outlet obstruction).

29. Have a family or personal history of medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) or multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) syndrome type 2.

30. Have a current or past history of chronic or acute pancreatitis.

31. Have acute or chronic hepatitis, or signs and symptoms of any other liver disease other than nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

32. Have a diagnosis or history of malignant disease within 5 years prior to baseline (Visit 2).

Exceptions:

 basal cell or squamous epithelial carcinomas of the skin that have been resected with no evidence of metastatic disease for 3 years, and 56  cervical carcinoma in situ that has been resected with no evidence of recurrence for at least 5 years prior to baseline (Visit 2).

33. Have a significant uncontrolled illness that in the opinion of the investigator may compromise the participant’s safety or interfere with interpretation of data; such illnesses or conditions include, but are not limited to  cerebrocardiovascular; for example, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, unstable arterial hypertension, moderate-to-severe (New York Heart Association class III/IV) heart failure, or cerebrovascular accident  respiratory  hepatic  renal  GI (excluding UC)  endocrine  hematologic or lymphoproliferative  neurologic  serious infection  awaiting or having a history of organ transplant (except keratoplasty), or  evidence of active vasculitis or uveitis.

34. Have a history of unstable major depressive disorder (MDD), suicidal ideation, or other severe psychiatric disorder (for example, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or other serious mood or anxiety disorder) within the last 2 years.

Note: Participants with MDD or generalized anxiety disorder whose disease state is considered stable for the past 2 years and expected to remain stable throughout the course of the study, in the opinion of the investigator, may be considered for inclusion.

35. Have a history of chronic alcohol abuse, IV drug abuse, or other illicit drug abuse within 1 year before screening colonoscopy.

36. Are, in the judgment of the investigator, actively suicidal and therefore deemed to be at significant risk for suicide.

37. Have answered “yes” to either Question 4 or Question 5 on the “Suicidal Ideation” portion of the C-SSRS and the ideation occurred within the past month.

OR Have answered “yes” to any of the suicide-related behaviors on the “suicidal behavior” portion of the C-SSRS and the behavior occurred within the past month.

38. Have had extra-abdominal surgery and have not recovered fully following surgery, including complete wound healing, before screening.

39. Have  a known or suspected allergy or hypersensitivity to mirikizumab or tirzepatide, any of their excipients, or any other GLP-1 receptor agonists or excipients, that would pose an unacceptable risk to the participant in this study  clinically significant multiple or severe drug allergies, or 57  a history of severe post-treatment hypersensitivity reactions, including, but not limited to, erythema multiforme major, linear IgA dermatosis, toxic epidermal necrolysis, or exfoliative dermatitis.

Infections and infectious disease

40. Have a current or recent acute, active infection. For at least 30 days before screening (Visit 1) and up to the randomization visit (Visit 2), participants must have no symptoms or signs of confirmed or suspected infection, and must have completed any appropriate anti-infective treatment.

Note: Participants who have an upper respiratory infection, a vaginal candida infection, or an oral candida infection and who are being treated only symptomatically and not requiring systemic anti-infectives may be considered for enrollment if other study eligibility criteria are met. Enrollment of participants with other uncomplicated local infections should be discussed with the sponsor’s designated medical monitor.

41. Have had any of the following types of infection, including chronic or recurring extraintestinal infections, within 3 months prior to the screening visit (Visit 1) or develops any of these infections before the randomization visit (Visit 2):

 Serious (requiring hospitalization, or IV or equivalent oral antibiotic treatment, or both)  Opportunistic (as defined in Winthrop et al. 2015) Note: Herpes zoster is considered active and ongoing until all vesicles are dry and crusted over.

 Chronic (duration of symptoms, signs, and/or treatment of 6 weeks or longer)  Recurring (including, but not limited to, herpes simplex, herpes zoster, recurring cellulitis, and chronic osteomyelitis).

Note: Participants with only recurrent mild and uncomplicated orolabial herpes, or genital herpes, or both may be discussed with the sponsor’s designated medical monitor and considered for enrollment if other study eligibility criteria are met.

42. Have a nonserious extraintestinal infection that is not adequately treated prior to screening and randomization.

Note: A participant who develops an extraintestinal infection during the screening period must be adequately treated before receiving study intervention.

43. Have active TB or untreated LTBI.

[43a] Have active TB (Section 8.2.10).

[43b] Have had LTBI that has not been treated with a complete course of appropriate therapy as defined by the WHO and the United States CDC, unless such treatment is underway (Section 8.2.10).

Note: Participants diagnosed with LTBI at screening may be allowed to re-screen for the study, provided they fulfil the criteria described in Section 8.2.10. Participants who have a documented history of completing an appropriate TB prophylaxis regimen with no history of risk of re-exposure since their treatments were completed and no evidence of active TB are eligible to participate in the study.

44. Have HIV infection.

45. Have a current infection with HBV; that is, positive for HBsAg and/or PCR positive for HBV DNA (Section 8.2.11).

46. Have a current infection with HCV; that is, positive for HCV RNA (Section 8.2.12).

47. Have a known active COVID-19 infection.

If a participant has signs/symptoms suggestive of COVID-19, they should undergo molecular (for example, PCR) testing to rule out SARS-CoV-2 infection. Participants who do not meet COVID-19 eligibility criteria must be screen failed and may only rescreen after they meet the following COVID-19 criteria:

 Symptomatic participants: At least 14 days have passed since recovery, defined as resolution of fever without use of antipyretics and improvement in symptoms  Asymptomatic participants: At least 14 days have passed since the first positive molecular (for example, PCR) test result.

48. Have C. difficile or other intestinal infection within 30 days of screening colonoscopy or test positive at screening for C. difficile or for other intestinal pathogens.

49. Have a confirmed diagnosis of cytomegalovirus-associated colitis.

Note: Participants may be eligible if they have had adequate treatment of this condition and have resolution of symptoms at least 3 months prior to screening colonoscopy, provided all other study eligibility criteria are met.

data.name: Lifestyle Considerations
data.text:
5.3.1.

Health Promotion and Lifestyle Program Per the SoA (Section 1.3), participants will consult a dietitian or nutritionist, or equivalent qualified designee or delegate* according to local standards, to receive lifestyle management counseling.(*Dietary counseling will be performed by a registered dietitian or nutritionist or equivalent qualified designee or delegate trained in collecting and assessing dietary intake and providing individualized dietary counseling according to the local standard).

62 Healthy dietary patterns and physical activity goals established during the lifestyle consultation and the importance of adherence to the lifestyle component of the study will be reinforced at each visit by site staff. Ensuring participants have optimal nutritional intake is highly recommended. In addition to Section 5.3.2, nutrition support and lifestyle resources are available in the investigator resources.

To encourage adherence, it is recommended that the participants complete their 3-day nutrition and physical activity log before each counseling visit. During each visit, the participant’s lifestyle behaviors are reviewed and advice to maximize adherence is provided as needed.

5.3.2.

Meals and Dietary Considerations Individualized counseling for a healthy dietary pattern At Visit 2 and subsequent visits, study participants will receive individualized counseling regarding a healthy dietary pattern with the goal of optimizing nutritional status while on pharmacotherapy. The counseling will be performed by a dietitian or nutritionist, or equivalent qualified designee, according to the local standard.

Counseling considerations The focus of the counseling should facilitate healthier dietary choices and promote mindful eating.

It should include instruction on customized nutrient-dense food and beverage choices to reflect personal preferences, cultural traditions, and budgetary considerations.

Consider the following principles in counseling sessions:

 Focus on high quality, nutrient rich, minimally processed foods. Limit foods high in solid fats, added sugar, and salt.

 Include fiber rich foods.

 For each meal (on an 8-10 inch [20-25 cm] plate), consider including approximately ½ plate of fruits/vegetables, ¼ plate of whole grains, and ¼ plate of protein. Incorporate 1 to 2 servings of healthy, unsaturated fats on most days (for example, nuts, avocado, olive oil, and salmon).

 Encourage participants to optimize daily protein intake to reach calculated daily protein goal based on ideal body weight and tailored to individual health and nutrition requirements. General daily recommended protein requirements are 60 to 120 g/day for women and 75 to 120 g/day for men. This should be individualized based on each participant’s unique needs such as medical conditions, physical activity levels, etc.

 Drink enough water and/or unsweetened or decaffeinated fluids to stay well hydrated.

Fluid intake of at least 2 L/day may be necessary for optimal hydration. Modifications to daily fluid amount should be individualized based on each participant’s unique needs such as medical conditions, hydration status, physical activity levels, etc.

 Follow hunger cues. If not feeling hungry, prioritize protein intake first, plan to eat smaller and more frequent (every 3-4 hours) meals/snacks and avoid skipping meals to meet daily nutrition requirements as calculated based on individual needs.

63 5.3.3.

Monitoring Nutritional Needs Caloric restriction is a standard component of weight-reduction interventions, and there is potential that a small portion of participants will have significantly reduced caloric intake.

Medical staff should monitor the participant’s nutritional and hydration status and attention should be given to ensure participants are eating high-quality foods that include adequate micronutrients and macronutrients. These recommendations should be personalized based on participants’ comprehensive medical conditions at the investigator’s discretion.

Consider additional assessment as described in Sections 8.2.13 and 10.2.2 if  the PI suspects the participant may have malnutrition, for example, caloric intake is significantly reduced to below 800 to 1200 kcal  a participant’s BMI falls below 22 kg/m2, or  in participants with T2DM, weight loss is >20% or >4 kg/month.

5.3.4.

Physical Activity At Visit 3 and all subsequent visits, participants will be advised regarding achieving a healthy physical activity level. At least 150 minutes per week of moderate intensity aerobic exercise, and muscle strengthening (resistance) exercise at least 3 times per week is recommended.

Counseling in lifestyle modification should be completed according to the SoA and must be documented in the participant’s medical record.

Activity before blood collections Participants will abstain from strenuous exercise for 24 hours before each blood collection for clinical laboratory tests.

5.3.5.

Blood Donation Study participants should be instructed not to donate blood or blood products during the study.

data.name: Screen Failures
data.text:
A screen failure occurs when a participant who consents to participate in the clinical study is not subsequently assigned to study intervention. A minimal set of screen failure information is required to ensure transparent reporting of screen failure participants to meet the CONSORT publishing requirements and to respond to queries from regulatory authorities. Minimal information includes demography, screen failure details, and any SAE.

Individuals who do not meet the criteria for participation in this study (screen failure) may be rescreened once or twice (see Section 5.4.2).

5.4.1.

Allowed Retesting of Screening Investigations These screening investigations can be retested 1 time at the discretion of the investigator:

 Screening hematology and chemistry blood tests: where results are outside the acceptable range for inclusion in the study but may be within the acceptable range for inclusion on retesting due to test-retest variability 64  Stool testing: if there is a technical difficulty in performing or reporting the C. difficile or stool culture assays (see Section 5.4.1.1)  Retesting or confirmatory testing with an IGRA: for example, QuantiFERON ®-TB Gold or T-SPOT ® assay (see Section 8.2.10)  Colonoscopy: where the endoscopist is unable to adequately visualize the mucosa, for example, due to poor bowel preparation or technical issues with equipment, or where the central reader is unable to determine the centrally read ES, for example, due to failure of the recording equipment.

The retesting described above is not considered rescreening.

Retesting of other screening investigations should be discussed with the sponsor’s designated medical monitor prior to retesting.

5.4.1.1.

Screening Stool Testing Stool culture Participants must have a negative stool culture from which no enteric pathogens are isolated to participate in the study.

Retesting is allowed within the screening period if there is a technical difficulty in performing or reporting the stool culture assay, as stated in Section 5.4.1.

Participants who have a “positive” stool culture result can be rescreened once, provided that the following conditions have been met:

 the participant has been adequately treated, and o if antibiotics were prescribed, participant has been off antibiotics for 30 days, or o if antibiotics were not prescribed, 30 days or more has elapsed since resolution of acute symptoms and signs associated with the underlying intestinal infection.

To confirm that the reason for screen failure (positive stool culture) has resolved, it is recommended that the investigator performs a local stool culture test before rescreening. Upon rescreen (Visit 1), a negative stool culture result from the central laboratory is required to meet this eligibility criterion.

Additional local stool culture/testing is allowed at the investigator’s discretion or based on country requirements.

C difficile toxin testing This assay tests for the presence of C. difficile toxin protein, followed by a confirmatory test for C. difficile toxin gene expression in the stool sample.

Participants should test negative for C. difficile to receive mirikizumab. Retesting is allowed within the same screening period if there is a technical difficulty in performing or reporting the C. difficile assays, or if in the judgment of the investigator, the participant’s symptoms or signs are not consistent with C. difficile infection.

Participants who test positive at screening for C. difficile can be rescreened once for the study, once they have been adequately treated and off antibiotics for 30 days.

65 Participants who have been adequately treated for C. difficile with fecal microbial transplantation or IV immunoglobulin therapy can be rescreened once for the study 30 days after completing their therapy.

To confirm that the reason for screen failure (positive C. difficile) has resolved, it is recommended that the investigator performs a local C. difficile test before rescreening. Upon rescreen (Visit 1), a negative C. difficile result from the central laboratory is required to meet this eligibility criterion.

5.4.2.

Rescreening of Individuals Who Fail Screening Informed consent for rescreening Each time an allowed rescreening is performed, the potential participant must sign a new ICF and will receive a new unique identifier (Sections 10.1.3 and 10.1.4).

Procedures not required to be repeated during rescreening If a participant’s protocol-required screening chest x-ray and TB tests were performed within 90 days before the date of signing the ICF for rescreening, these procedures are not required to be repeated. However, these procedures can be repeated at the discretion of the investigator.

Authorized as defined by EU Clinical Trial Regulation Authorized and not used according to EU authorizationa Authorized and not used according to EU authorizationb Not authorized in EU Abbreviations: EU = European Union; IV = intravenous; Q4W = every 4 weeks; QW = every week; SC = subcutaneous; T2DM = type 2 diabetes mellitus; UC = ulcerative colitis.

67 Packaging and labeling Study interventions will be supplied by the sponsor or its designee in accordance with current Good Manufacturing Practice. Study interventions will be labeled as appropriate for country requirements.

6.1.1.

Participant Monitoring and Observation After Study Intervention Initial monitoring and observation Participants will be monitored for 1 hour after IV administration of mirikizumab. Longer monitoring is allowed when required by investigator practice or local standard of care. Sites must have resuscitation equipment, emergency medications, and appropriately trained personnel available during the infusion and post-infusion monitoring period.

In addition, participants should be observed after tirzepatide dosing at randomization (Visit 2) and the initial administration of mirikizumab SC at the investigator’s discretion for any AEs.

Subsequent monitoring and observation Subsequent monitoring and observation will be performed according to investigator practice or local standard of care.

6.1.2.

Self-Administration Training and Dosing Diary Training for tirzepatide self-administration Site personnel will train the participant and/or caregiver to administer tirzepatide using a prefilled syringe at Visit 2. It is strongly recommended that the trained participant or caregiver administers the first dose of tirzepatide at Visit 2 under supervision of the site personnel.

Thereafter, study intervention should be administered by the participant or caregiver. If additional training is necessary, an injection may be administered by the participant and/or caregiver under the supervision of the site personnel. If the participant or their caregiver do not feel comfortable administering the injection, it can be done by the study personnel. The site personnel must document in the source documents that injection training has been provided to the participant or caregiver verbally and in written form at the first dispensing visit. Refresher training will be provided as needed throughout the study. Injection training is the responsibility of the investigator or other qualified staff.

Training for mirikizumab self-administration In this protocol, self-administration is defined as the SC injection of 200 mg mirikizumab, where either the participant injects themselves or a caregiver administers the injection to the participant.

Site personnel will train the participant and/or caregiver to administer mirikizumab SC using prefilled syringes at Visit 5.

For considerations regarding observation of the first self-administration and documentation of mirikizumab injection training, see subsection “Training for tirzepatide self-administration.” 68 Dosing diary Dosing diary will be dispensed to each participant as indicated in the SoA, for recording pertinent data about each injection.

6.1.3.

Timing and Location of Doses Timing of concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide or mirikizumab and placebo When both study interventions are due on the same date, it is recommended that they are administered within a reasonable time frame from each other (that is, around the same time of day, such as both in the morning) and in a different location (see “Dosing locations” subsection).

During mirikizumab induction dosing, it is recommended that the administration of tirzepatide or placebo occur at least 30 minutes after the end of the mirikizumab infusion. Refer to the appropriate directions for use provided by the sponsor for the study intervention.

Timing of doses for tirzepatide There are no restrictions on the time of day each weekly dose of tirzepatide is given, but it is advisable to administer the tirzepatide injections on the same day and time each week, with or without meals.

If a dose of tirzepatide is missed, the participant must take it as soon as possible within 4 days (96 hours) after the missed dose. If more than 4 days have passed, that dose must be skipped and the next dose must be taken on the regular scheduled day. In each case, participants can then resume their regular QW dosing schedule.

Timing of doses for mirikizumab There are no restrictions on the time of day each Q4W dose of mirikizumab is given. If a mirikizumab SC dose is missed, administer it as soon as possible and resume dosing Q4W thereafter. If the participant has a scheduled visit >14 days from the last administered dose, continue dosing per the original dosing schedule per the SoA.

Dosing locations For both tirzepatide and SC administration of mirikizumab, injection sites include  the abdomen (stomach area)  thigh (upper leg), and  back of the upper arm.

Participants will self-inject the SC study intervention in the abdomen or thigh.

If the injection is given by somebody else, they will administer the injection either in the upper arm, abdomen, or thigh.

When mirikizumab and tirzepatide are administered concomitantly, use an anatomically distinct site on the opposite side of the body for injecting each study intervention; for example, if mirikizumab is injected in the right side of the abdomen, tirzepatide should be injected in the left thigh or the back of the left upper arm. Do not inject in areas where the skin is tender, bruised, erythematous, or indurated.

69 A new prefilled syringe will be used for each SC injection.

6.1.4.

Dose Escalation 6.1.4.1.

Mirikizumab No dose escalations are applicable.

6.1.4.2.

Tirzepatide Tirzepatide treatment will follow a fixed dose-escalation as follows:

 the starting dose will be 2.5 mg QW. After 4 weeks, the dose is increased to 5 mg, and  dose is increased by 2.5 mg Q4W until the 15-mg dose is reached or to the highest maintenance dose tolerated by the participant (5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg).
