data.name: Preparation, Handling, Storage, and Accountability
data.text:
Sponsor or its designee will supply study intervention to the investigator for dispensing at Visit 2.

The investigator or designee must confirm appropriate storage conditions have been maintained during transit for all study intervention received and any discrepancies are reported and resolved before use of the study intervention.

Only participants enrolled in the study may receive study intervention. Only authorized study personnel may supply, prepare, or administer study intervention.

At the study site, all study intervention must be stored in a secure, environmentally controlled, and monitored (manual or automated) area in accordance with the labeled storage conditions with access limited to the investigator and authorized study personnel. For off-site (at-home) administration, sponsor will provide storage instructions.

The investigator or authorized study personnel are responsible for study intervention accountability, reconciliation, and record maintenance, that is, receipt, reconciliation, and final disposition records.

Further guidance and information for the final disposition of unused study interventions are provided in the Pharmacy Manual.

data.name: Assignment to Study Intervention
data.text:
Method of treatment assignment All eligible participants will be centrally assigned to randomized study intervention using the IWRS. Before the study is initiated, the login information and directions for the IWRS will be provided to each site.

Randomization ratios and stratification factors Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the  mirikizumab and placebo treatment arm, or  mirikizumab and tirzepatide concomitant administration treatment arm.

The randomization will be stratified by  sex (AFAB vs. AMAB) Note: The randomly assigned study population will include up to approximately 70% of either individuals AFAB or AMAB, whoever enrolls faster. The remaining sex will make up the remainder of the participant population.

 BMI ≥27 kg/m 2 to <30 kg/m 2 versus ≥30 kg/m 2  previous advanced therapy failure status (yes/no), and  baseline disease activity (mMS: [5-6] or [7-9]).

71 For participants with BMI ≥27 kg/m 2 to <30 kg/m 2, the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbid condition is required to be randomized.

data.name: Blinding
data.text:
Mirikizumab treatment will be open label.

Tirzepatide treatment, and matching placebo, will be blinded for both study participants and study personnel.

Emergency unblinding Emergency unblinding for AEs may be performed through the IWRS. This option may be used ONLY if the participant’s well-being requires knowledge of the participant’s treatment assignment. All actions resulting in an unblinding event are recorded and reported by the IWRS.

If, because of emergency unblinding, a participant’s tirzepatide assignment is unblinded to the participant or to blinded site personnel who are performing study assessments, including the investigator, the participant must be discontinued from tirzepatide (Section 7.1.1).

In case of an emergency, the investigator has the sole responsibility for determining if unblinding of a participants’ intervention assignment is warranted. Participant safety must always be the first consideration in making such a determination. If the investigator decides that unblinding is warranted, it is the responsibility of the investigator to promptly document the decision and rationale and notify the sponsor as soon as possible.

data.name: Study Intervention Compliance
data.text:
When the participant and/or caregiver administers study intervention(s) at home, compliance with study interventions will be assessed at visits indicated in the SoA (Section 1.3). Compliance will be assessed by  direct questioning  counting of unused study drug and/or empty cartons returned  review of the dosing diary, and  documented in the source documents.

Participants will be instructed to return any unused prefilled syringes at the times specified in the SoA.

Treatment compliance for each visit interval is defined as taking at least 75% of the required doses of study interventions. Similarly, a participant will be considered significantly noncompliant if he or she is judged by the investigator to have intentionally or repeatedly taken more than the prescribed amount of medication (more than 125%).

In addition to the assessment of a participant’s compliance with the study intervention administration, other aspects of compliance with the study treatments will be assessed at each visit based on  the participant’s adherence to the visit schedule  completion of the dosing diary, and  any other parameters the investigator considers necessary.

72 Participants considered to be poorly compliant with their medication and/or the study procedures will receive additional training and instruction, as required, and will be reminded of the importance of complying with the protocol.

A record of the number of mirikizumab, placebo, and tirzepatide prefilled syringes dispensed to and taken by each participant must be maintained and reconciled with study intervention and compliance records. The date and time of each dose administered, location of administration, and reason if dose was not administered will be recorded in the dosing diary.

data.name: Dose Modification
data.text:
6.6.1.

Mirikizumab Dose modification is not applicable to mirikizumab in this study.

6.6.2.

Tirzepatide For dose escalation information, refer to Section 6.1.4.2.

During the dose-escalation period, the investigator should make every effort to escalate participants to the MTD and continue participants on this dose for the duration of the treatment period.

Dose modification for tirzepatide is not permitted, except for management of  intolerable GI symptoms (Section 6.6.2.1), and  participants with perceived excessive weight reduction (Section 6.6.2.2).

6.6.2.1.

Management of Participants with Gastrointestinal Symptoms The dose-escalation scheme is designed to minimize the development of intolerable GI symptoms. As stated in the table below, participants who experience intolerable GI symptoms (for example, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea) at any time during the study, should first be counselled on dietary behaviors that may help mitigate nausea and vomiting, for example, eating smaller meals, splitting 3 daily meals into 4 or more smaller ones, and stopping eating when they feel full. If symptoms persist, the participant should be prescribed, at the investigator’s discretion, symptomatic medication, for example, anti-emetic or anti-diarrheal medication temporarily. Prior to initiation of anti-diarrheal and while on anti-diarrheal medication, participants should be evaluated for signs of concurrent infection or colonic dilation. For any worsening of GI symptoms, investigators should also consider evaluating for a flare/worsening of a participant’s UC. This may include evaluating for C. difficile infection, objective evidence of a disease flare and toxic megacolon.

A temporary interruption of study drug for 1 dose is permitted, provided the participant has taken the last 3 weekly dose. If the participant responds to symptomatic medications, study treatment should be resumed at the assigned dose immediately, either alone or in combination with symptomatic medication, which can also be utilized to manage symptoms. If intolerable GI symptoms persist despite the above measures, the investigator should consider dose de-escalation with subsequent re-escalation and may contact the sponsor for questions. A maximum of 2 dose de-escalation or re-escalations per participant will be permitted during the study. If intolerable GI symptoms persist despite dietary counseling, symptomatic treatment, temporary drug 73 interruption for one dose, and resumption at a lower dose of study drug, the participant should be discontinued from tirzepatide and consider evaluating the participant for UC exacerbation. All participants who discontinue tirzepatide should continue to attend scheduled study visits. All dose adjustments will be managed through IWRS.

This table summarizes steps the investigator should follow to mitigate GI symptoms (for example, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea) at any time during the study for the tirzepatide intervention group.

Management of participants with intolerable GI AEs Step Guidance Step 1 Advise participants to eat smaller meals, for example, splitting 3 daily meals into 4 or more smaller meals, and to stop eating when they feel full and avoiding foods that trigger symptoms.

Step 2 Continue STEP 1 + If symptoms persist, treat with symptomatic medication, for example, anti-emetic or anti-diarrheal medication temporarily, per local availability and individual participant needs. Use of symptomatic medication should be captured as concomitant medication in the CRF.

Step 3 Continue STEP 1 + STEP 2 + If Steps 1 and 2 do not alleviate intolerable GI symptoms during the first 40 weeks of the study, consider temporary interruption of tirzepatide. Temporary interruption of tirzepatide is defined as  omission of 1 tirzepatide dose, and  taken the last 3 weekly doses The data related to temporary interruption of study treatment should be documented in source documents and entered on the CRF.

In these instances, the participant will only hold tirzepatide; mirikizumab may be administered as scheduled. Participant should be on stable maintenance dose from Week 40 through Week 52.

After the interruption, the investigator should restart the dose or escalate the dose as required, with the participant taking medication to alleviate their GI symptoms. If tirzepatide is temporarily interrupted for 2 or more consecutive doses, please refer to Section 7.1.2 for restart instructions.

The data pertaining to temporary interruption of study intervention should be documented in source documents.

Note: When restarting tirzepatide, the study personnel should notify the sponsor at least 2 weeks before the dosing visit to ensure adequate intervention supply at the site.

Step 4 If intolerable GI symptoms persist despite the above measures, the investigator should consider dose de-escalation with subsequent re-escalation and may contact the sponsor for questions.

6.6.2.2.

Management of Participants with Perceived Excessive Weight Reduction If participants reach a BMI ≤22 kg/m2 any time during the study, the investigator or designated provider should initially evaluate the participant’s dietary intake to confirm that the participant is meeting dietary intake guidance.

For participants who have perceived excessive weight loss or have reached a BMI of ≤22 kg/m2 and if there are concerns that the degree of body weight reduction may lead to participant decision to discontinue from study intervention, the investigator should contact the sponsor to consider a tirzepatide dose reduction as outlined in Section 6.6.2.3.

data.name: Treatment of Overdose
data.text:
For this study, any dose of study intervention greater than the specified number of injections assigned through randomization will be considered an overdose. Tirzepatide overdose is defined as any amount of tirzepatide over the intended dose in less than 72 hours.

Refer to the mirikizumab and tirzepatide IBs and product labeling for further information.

In the event of an overdose, the investigator or treating physician should:

 contact the medical monitor immediately  evaluate the participant to determine, in consultation with the medical monitor, whether study intervention should be interrupted or whether the dose should be reduced  closely monitor the participant for any AE or SAE and laboratory abnormalities as medically appropriate until, for example, study intervention no longer has a clinical effect and report the overdose event as an AE and document it, and  initiate appropriate supportive treatment according to the participant’s clinical signs and symptoms.

data.name: Prior and Concomitant Therapy
data.text:
6.9.1.

General Considerations Participants should be instructed to consult authorized site personnel before taking any new medications or supplements during the study.

Authorized site personnel should consult the sponsor’s designated medical monitor if there are any questions about concomitant therapies during the study.

Participants are permitted to use concomitant medications that they require during the study, except certain medications specifically excluded in the protocol (Section 5.2) and those that may interfere with the assessment of efficacy and safety characteristics of the study interventions (Sections 6.9.2 and 5.2).

77 Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying and, thereby, has the potential to impact the absorption of concomitantly administered oral medications. Caution should be exercised when oral medications are concomitantly administered with tirzepatide. Monitor participants on oral medications dependent on threshold concentrations for efficacy and those with a narrow therapeutic index (for example, warfarin) when concomitantly administered with tirzepatide.

Concomitant therapy data collection Any medication or vaccine, including over-the-counter or prescription medicines, vitamins, and/or herbal supplements, or other specific categories of interest, that the participant is receiving at the time of enrollment or receives during the study must be recorded along with the  reason for use  dates of administration including start and end dates, and  dosage information including dose and frequency for concomitant therapy of special interest.

For this study, the concomitant medications of special interest include  antihyperglycemic medications (Section 6.9.2), and  prior treatments for IBD (Section 5.2, inclusion criteria [10] and [11], and Sections 6.9.4 and 10.8).

The medical monitor should be contacted if there are any questions regarding concomitant or prior therapy.

6.9.2.

Concomitant Antihyperglycemic Medications After randomization, discontinuation, dose modification, or formulation change of anti- hyperglycemic medications would be at the guidance of primary physician or healthcare provider qualified to manage diabetes mellitus.

Participants with T2DM are allowed to use concomitant antihyperglycemic medications that they require during the study, except  sulfonylurea medications  amylin mimetics  DPP-4 inhibitors  GLP-1 receptor agonists  GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists  glinides, and  insulin.

Antihyperglycemic medications for the management of T2DM are permitted; for example, metformin, thiazolidinediones, and SGLT2 inhibitors.

Participants who develop persistent severe hyperglycemia as determined by the investigator or healthcare provider caring for participant’s diabetes may be candidates for addition of or dose increase in permitted antihyperglycemic therapies. The choice of new antihyperglycemic therapy (with the exception of amylin mimetics, GLP-1 receptor agonists, GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists, 78 DPP-4 inhibitors, glinides, insulin, or sulfonylureas) or amount of dose increase will be at the discretion of the investigator or the participant’s usual diabetes care physician, according to local guidelines for treatment of T2DM.

Management and reporting of incident diabetes Participants will be monitored throughout the study for incident diabetes. If, in the opinion of the investigator, incident diabetes is suspected or occurs after randomization, participant should be monitored by investigator or referred to healthcare provider with appropriate specialization in management of diabetes per local guidelines. In general, diabetes mellitus is considered if HbA1c ≥6.5%, random plasma glucose ≥200 mg/dL, or diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (ADA 2024).

Participants who develop diabetes during the study will be educated on the signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia and its treatment, and monitor hypoglycemic episodes as directed by local standard of care under direction of the participant’s healthcare professional. Any event of hypoglycemia should be reported to the site.

6.9.3.

Prohibited Concomitant Medications For prohibited antihyperglycemic medications, see Section 6.9.2. For other prohibited concomitant medications, see Section 5.2.

Administration of prohibited UC medications, approved or investigational, is not allowed. The use of such medications should not be withheld if, in the opinion of the investigator, failure to prescribe them would compromise participant safety. Participants who require a prohibited medication to treat their UC must be discontinued from study intervention (Section 7.1.1).

A participant who requires a prohibited medication for a non-UC indication should be discussed with the sponsor’s designated medical monitor. A participant who initiates a prohibited medication for a non-UC indication may either discontinue the study intervention (Section 7.1.1) or discontinue the prohibited medication.

If a concomitant medication is needed to treat an AE or for appropriate medical management, the investigator should base decisions on the participant and clinical factors, considering prohibited medications.

6.9.4.

Permitted Concomitant Medications For permitted antihyperglycemic medications, see Section 6.9.2.

Participants should maintain their usual medication regimens for concurrent conditions or diseases throughout the study, unless those medications are specifically excluded (Section 5.2).

Participants taking permitted prescription UC concomitant medications, other than oral corticosteroids, are to keep the doses stable unless modifications are needed due to AEs or dose modification is specified in Section 10.8.

Continued use of nonprescription herbal supplements or medicines that are taken specifically for the treatment of UC should be discussed with the sponsor’s designated medical monitor.

79 Monitoring of participants enrolled on 6-MP and azathioprine The sponsor recommends monitoring the thiopurine metabolites levels of 6TG and 6-MMP for any participants enrolled on 6-MP and azathioprine. The rationale for this recommendation includes (Klein et al. 2024):

 Slower gastric and duodenal transit time, mainly due to the GLP-1 receptor agonist effects, may allow for increased 6-MP absorption.

 Anti-inflammatory properties of GLP-1 receptor agonist may augment bowel healing and facilitate improved thiopurine absorption.

 A patient’s weight loss on GLP-1 therapy such as tirzepatide may affect weight-based dosing.

6.9.5.

Corticosteroid Use and Taper Local administration of corticosteroids, for example, intranasal, inhaled, intra-articular, or topical, is allowed (Section 10.8).

Participants who enter the study on oral corticosteroid therapy for treatment of UC should maintain a stable dose of corticosteroid during the first 12 weeks of treatment.

Corticosteroid tapering will be initiated at Week 12. For participants who cannot tolerate the corticosteroid taper without recurrence of clinical symptoms, corticosteroid taper may be paused, or the corticosteroid dose may be increased back to the original dose at induction baseline, but not higher. If doses higher than baseline are needed, consult the sponsor’s designated medical monitor.

In situations where the steroid tapering is paused, the tapering regimen described below should be reinitiated within 2 weeks of interruption of taper, if possible, with a goal to complete tapering no later than Week 24.

The recommended tapering schedule for oral corticosteroids (other than budesonide extended -release tablets [budesonide MMX] or beclomethasone dipropionate [gastro-resistant prolonged release tablet]) is as follows.

 Dose >10 mg per day prednisone or equivalent: taper daily dose by 5 mg per week until receiving 10 mg per day, and then continue tapering at 2.5 mg per week until 0 mg per day.

 Dose ≤10 mg per day prednisone or equivalent: taper daily dose by 2.5 mg per week until 0 mg per day.

The recommended tapering schedule for oral budesonide MMX (up to 9 mg per day) is to decrease frequency of tablets from daily to every other day for 2 weeks, followed by every third day for 2 weeks, and then discontinue.

The recommended tapering schedule for participants receiving oral beclomethasone dipropionate (gastro-resistant prolonged-release tablet) (up to 5 mg per day) is to reduce tablets to 5 mg every other day for 4 weeks, and then discontinue.

80 6.9.6.

Disease Progression and Rescue Therapy The participants with exacerbations of their UC symptoms will have an opportunity to be evaluated at a scheduled or unscheduled visit for UC disease worsening. Worsening of underlying UC will be defined at a scheduled or unscheduled visit based on  evaluation of symptoms in electronic diary entries, hematology, chemistry, C-reactive protein, fecal calprotectin, and calculation of the combined stool frequency and rectal bleeding score in UC, and  exclusion of other causes of worsening disease activity unrelated to underlying UC, such as infections.

At the investigator’s discretion, to further evaluate a potential worsening of underlying UC, flexible sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy may be scheduled if the most recent flexible endoscopy or colonoscopy was ≥4 weeks prior to the visit during which worsening was evaluated.

Investigators and participants may opt to intensify care through unscheduled visits. The investigators also have the discretion to have the participant discontinue mirikizumab or the study. However, this study will not include rescue therapy.

81

data.name: Discontinuation of Study Intervention
data.text:
Continuing in the study after discontinuation of study intervention When necessary, a participant may be permanently discontinued from study intervention, per investigator’s decision. If so, the participant will discontinue the study intervention (treatment) and will remain in the study and follow procedures for all remaining study visits, as shown in the SoA (Section 1.3).

Further, study discontinuation criteria allow for the participants to be discontinued at any time by investigator or by the decision of participant if they are receiving insufficient benefit from study therapy or require treatment with another therapeutic agent that has been demonstrated to be effective for the treatment of UC.

If the participant is unwilling or unable to return for all applicable study visits, the site should attempt to collect as much follow-up information as possible, especially data collection pertaining to primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints at Week 52 of the treatment period.

7.1.1.

Permanent Discontinuation of Study Intervention Unless indicated otherwise, if a participant meets the criteria for permanent discontinuation, both mirikizumab and tirzepatide should be stopped.

A participant may be permanently discontinued from the study intervention for the following reasons:

 Suicidal ideation and behavior: The participant o answered “yes” to Question 4 or Question 5 on the “Suicidal Ideation” portion of the C-SSRS, or o answered “yes” to any of the suicide-related behaviors on the “Suicidal Behavior” portion of the C-SSRS.

Note: A psychiatrist or appropriately trained professional may assist in the decision to discontinue the participant.

 Depression symptoms: If the participant has a QIDS-SR16 score greater than or equal to 16 on the total score or greater than or equal to 2 on Item 12, the investigator may decide to withhold study intervention or discontinue study intervention. A mental health care professional may assist in the decision.

 Hypersensitivity reactions: If the investigator determines that a systemic hypersensitivity reaction has occurred related to study intervention administration, the participant may be permanently discontinued from the study intervention, and the sponsor’s designated medical monitor should be notified. If the investigator is uncertain about whether a systemic hypersensitivity reaction has occurred and whether 82 discontinuation of study intervention is warranted, the investigator may consult the sponsor.

 Malnutrition: If the participant develops severe or persistent malnutrition, refractory to treatment despite nutritional guidance and supplementation, consider discontinuing tirzepatide, and discuss management of the participant with the sponsor-designated monitor.

A participant must be permanently discontinued from the study intervention for the following reasons:

 Participant decision: The participant requests to discontinue study intervention.

The reason(s) for the decision will be documented.

 Investigator decision o the investigator decides that the participant should be discontinued from the study medication for safety reasons  The participant develops anaphylaxis to study intervention.

 The participant is AFAB and of childbearing potential, sexually active, and does not agree to follow the effective contraception defined in Section 10.4.1.

 The participant requires treatment for exacerbation of UC with medication(s) o at doses higher than those specified in inclusion criterion [11], for example, prednisone >20 mg/day, or o with prohibited medications specified in the exclusion criterion [50], for example, a course of IV corticosteroids, a single dose of infliximab, or IV cyclosporine.

 The participant requires a colectomy, proctocolectomy, or partial colectomy during the study.

 The participant has bariatric surgery.

 The participant has current evidence of an adenomatous polyp with high-grade dysplasia.

 If the participant’s BMI falls below 19 kg/m2 during the study, the participant must be discontinued from tirzepatide.

 Unblinding: If an investigator, site personnel performing assessments, or participant is unblinded from tirzepatide treatment, the participant must be discontinued from the tirzepatide. In cases where there are ethical reasons to have the participant continue on study intervention, the investigator must obtain specific approval from the sponsor or designee for the participant to continue in the study.

 The participant develops significant GI symptoms despite management (Section 6.6.2.1).

Note: The investigator should contact the sponsor to discuss whether it is medically appropriate for the participant to continue tirzepatide.

83  The participant develops any of these diagnoses or conditions during the study:

o T1DM o T2DM requiring insulin o new onset diabetic retinopathy requiring therapy o intolerable GI symptoms that do not respond to mitigations outlined in Section 6.6.2.1 o MTC after randomization o acute or chronic pancreatitis, confirmed by adjudication, or o HBV or HCV: The participant tests positive for HBV DNA (Section 8.2.11) or tests positive for HCV RNA (Section 8.2.12). For additional criteria for permanent discontinuation of mirikizumab, see Section 8.2.11.

Note: The HBV DNA result is to be confirmed if initial positive test result is positive but below the level of quantification (Section 8.2.11). Prior to discontinuation of any immunomodulatory and/or immunosuppressive therapy, including mirikizumab, the participant is to be referred to, evaluated, and managed by a specialist physician with expertise in evaluation and management of viral hepatitis. The timing of discontinuation from study intervention relative to the initiation of any antiviral treatment for hepatitis is to be based on the recommendation of the consulting specialist physician, in conjunction with the investigator, and aligned with medical guidelines and standard of care.

 certain AEs:

o the participant develops HIV infection o the participant develops active TB or has untreated LTBI (Section 8.2.10)  The participant experiences an AE or SAE that, in the opinion of the investigator or sponsor, would preclude them from continuing to receive study drug.

 The participant is diagnosed with malignancy, except for successfully treated basal or squamous cell skin carcinoma.

 The participant develops any condition or contraindication as addressed in the local labelling for mirikizumab or tirzepatide that would preclude the participant from continuing the study intervention.

 If the participant, for any reason, requires treatment with another therapeutic agent that is prohibited by this study (see Section 5.2) and has been demonstrated to be effective for the treatment of UC, obesity, or overweight, discontinuation from study intervention occurs prior to introduction of new agent.

 If the participant is noncompliant with study procedures and/or study intervention administration, the investigator should assess the participant to determine the reason for noncompliance and educate and/or manage the participant as appropriate to improve compliance. If in consultation with sponsor or its designee, the noncompliance is deemed significant, discontinue participant from the study.

84  If the participant has any of the following results on 2 consecutive samples taken at least 48 hours, but no more than 1 week, apart:

Test Result Absolute neutrophil count <500 cells/μL (<0.5 x 103/μL or <0.50 GI/L) Absolute lymphocyte count <200 cells/μL (<0.2 x 103/μL or <0.2 GI/L) Total WBC <1000 cells/μL (<1.0 x 103/μL) Hemoglobin <6.5 g/dL (<65 g/L) 7.1.2.

Temporary Discontinuation Temporary discontinuation of both study interventions In certain situations, after randomization, the investigator may need to temporarily interrupt study interventions. Every effort should be made by the investigator to maintain participants on study intervention and to restart study intervention after any temporary interruption, as soon as it is safe to do so. The investigator should provide guidance to the participant, to consult before any dose interruption, and evaluate participant status prior to resumption.

Cases that may merit temporary withholding of the study intervention should be discussed with the medical monitor. The medical monitor, in consultation with the investigator, will determine when it is appropriate to recommence study intervention.

Both study interventions must be temporarily discontinued if the participant:

 requires major surgery Note: Administration of the study intervention may be restarted only after adequate wound healing.

 develops depression symptoms (see Section 7.1.1) Temporary interruption of tirzepatide This table describes how to manage treatment if there is a temporary interruption of tirzepatide study intervention. This may require an additional unscheduled visit to address in a timely manner.

If study intervention interruption is… Then….

2 consecutive doses or less participant restarts study intervention at the last dosage taken prior to the interruption and continues escalation, as per escalation schedule (Section 6.1.4.2). If the dose interruption occurred immediately prior to a scheduled dose-escalation visit, the participant should proceed with the next escalation.

3 consecutive doses or more participant restarts study intervention at 5 mg and repeats dose-escalation scheme.

85 due to an AE the event is to be documented and followed according to the procedures in Section 8.3 of this protocol.

due to intolerable persistent GI AE participant should be treated as suggested in Section 6.6.2.1.

Temporary discontinuation of mirikizumab If participant meets these criteria… Then… Infection-related criteria A clinically important extraintestinal or intestinal infection (see exclusion criteria [40-49]) Withhold mirikizumab until resolution of all acute clinical signs and symptoms, and complete of all appropriate anti- infective treatment. If participant is diagnosed with LTBI, see Section 8.2.10 and the discontinuation criterion immediately below.

For infections requiring permanent discontinuation, see Section 7.1.1 for further details.

A diagnosis of LTBI during the study Permanently discontinue from mirikizumab unless the participant is a candidate for LTBI treatment, and is treated for LTBI as follows:

 Mirikizumab is temporarily held for at least the first 4 weeks of LTBI treatment.

 After receiving at least 4 weeks of appropriate LTBI therapy (as per WHO or US CDC guidelines), if there is no evidence of hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST must remain ≤2 times ULN) or other treatment intolerance, mirikizumab may be resumed.

 The participant must complete appropriate LTBI therapy to remain eligible to receive study mirikizumab.

HBV DNA results that are reported as positive, or as detecting HBV DNA, but HBV DNA is below the level of quantification See Section 8.2.11.

86 Neutrophil-related criteria Development of neutrophil and lymphocyte abnormalities during the study:

 a confirmed absolute neutrophil count <1 x 109/L (<1 x 103/μL or <1 GI/L; 2 assessments below this threshold)  absolute lymphocyte count <500 cells/μL (<0.5 x 103/μL or <0.50 GI/L) After the first retest confirming absolute lymphocyte count <0.5 x 103/μL (second assessment below threshold)  discontinue AZA, 6-MP, or MTX, if applicable, and  hold the next dose of mirikizumab.

The participant must be retested in approximately 2 weeks.

If the absolute lymphocyte count remains <0.5 x 103/L, repeat the hematology again in 2 weeks; that is, prior to the next dose of mirikizumab. If the absolute lymphocyte count still remains <0.5 x 103/L, the next dose of mirikizumab will not be administered. The participant must be retested again in 2 weeks.

If the absolute lymphocyte count still remains <0.5 x 103/L, mirikizumab will be permanently discontinued (Section 7.1.1). White blood cell and lymphocyte counts will be followed for these participants until they return to an acceptable level.

7.1.3.

Hepatic Criteria for Study Drug Interruption or Discontinuation See Section 8.2.9.3 for hepatic criteria for study intervention interruption or discontinuation.

See Section 10.5 for further guidance on hepatic monitoring.

data.name: Participant Discontinuation/Withdrawal from the Study
data.text:
Discontinuation is expected to be uncommon. To minimize the amount of missing data and to enable assessment of study objectives as planned in the study protocol, every attempt will be made to keep participants in the study regardless of study intervention use.

A participant must be discontinued from the study intervention and withdrawn from the study if the participant becomes pregnant during the study.

A participant may withdraw from the study  at any time at the participant’s own request for any reason or without providing any reason  at the discretion of the investigator for safety, behavioral, compliance, or administrative reasons, or  if enrolled in any other clinical study involving an investigational product, or enrolled in any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

At the time of discontinuing from the study, if possible, the participant will complete procedures for an EDV and post-treatment safety follow-up, as shown in the SoA. If the participant has not already discontinued the study intervention, the participant will be permanently discontinued from the study intervention at the time of the decision to discontinue the study.

If the participant withdraws consent for disclosure of future information, the sponsor may retain and continue to use any data collected before such a withdrawal of consent. If a participant 87 withdraws from the study, the participant may request destruction of any samples taken and not tested, and the investigator must document this in the site study records.

data.name: Lost to Follow-Up
data.text:
A participant will be considered lost to follow-up if they repeatedly fail to return for scheduled visits and are unable to be contacted by the study site. Site personnel or designee are expected to make diligent attempts to contact participants who fail to return for a scheduled visit or were otherwise unable to be followed up by the site.

data.name: Efficacy Assessments
data.text:
This table defines the UC-specific endpoints.

Endpoint Definition Clinical remission mMS of 0 to 2, including the following 3 components  SF subscore = 0 or 1  RB subscore = 0  Centrally read ES = 0 or 1; score of 1 modified to exclude friability Maintenance of clinical remission Achieving clinical remission at both Week 24 and Week 52 Corticosteroid-free remission Corticosteroid-free remission at Week 52 defined as:

 Clinical remission at Week 52, and  No corticosteroid use for ≥12 weeks prior to Week 52 Endoscopic response ES = 0 or 1, excluding friability Endoscopic remission ES = 0 Clinical response  Decrease in the mMS of ≥2 points and ≥30% decrease from baseline, and  decrease of ≥1 point in the RB subscore from baseline or an RB subscore of 0 or 1 Symptomatic response ≥30% decrease from baseline in the composite clinical endpoint of the sum of SF and RB subscores Symptomatic remission  SF subscore = 0 or 1 and  RB subscore = 0 Histologic improvement Geboes score ≤3.1; neutrophil infiltration in <5% of crypts; no crypt destruction; and no erosions, ulcerations, or granulation tissue Histologic remission Geboes score ≤2B.0: no lamina propria neutrophils; no neutrophils in the surface or crypt epithelium; no crypt destruction; and no erosions, ulcerations, or granulation tissue histologic-endoscopic mucosal improvement plus absence of neutrophils Achieving both  histologic remission (as defined above), and  endoscopic remission (as defined above) Bowel Urgency remission Urgency NRS = 0 or 1 89 8.1.1.

Primary Efficacy Assessments Primary endpoint As stated in Section 3, the primary endpoint is the proportion of participants who simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 52.

Clinical remission is defined in Section 8.1.

Methods for measuring body weight are described in Section 10.9.

8.1.1.1.

mMS The mMS (as provided in the FDA Guidance 2016) is a composite instrument reported by patients and the physician and is comprised of the following 3 subscores:

 Stool Frequency (SF)  Rectal Bleeding (RB), and  Endoscopic Subscore (ES).

Stool Frequency (SF) The SF subscore is a patient-reported measure. This item reports the number of stools in a 24-hour period, relative to the normal number of stools for that participant in the same period, on a 4-point scale (see Section 10.11). A stool is defined as a trip to the toilet when the participant:

 has a bowel movement, or  passes o blood alone, or o blood and mucus, or o mucus only.

The reference “normal SF” for each participant will be recorded in the eDiary at the screening visit. Normal SF for each participant is based on  reported SF when the participant was in remission, or  reported SF before initial onset of signs and symptoms of UC.

Remission refers to a period of time since being diagnosed with UC when the participant is not experiencing any signs or symptoms relating to UC. This period of time may last a few weeks or a few months or may even last several years.

Rectal Bleeding (RB) The RB subscore is a patient-reported measure. This item reports the most severe amount of blood passed with stool for a given day, on a 4-point scale (see Section 10.11).

Endoscopic Subscore (ES) The ES is a physician-reported measure that indicates the worst appearance of the mucosa on flexible sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy, on a 4-point scale. Determination of the ES is further detailed in Section 10.11.

Consistent with current clinical practice and regulatory advice, this study excludes friability from the definition of an ES of 1. Also consistent with best clinical trial practice, endoscopy scores will be determined from blinded central readers.

90 The local endoscopy score is collected on paper and should be transcribed immediately, no more than 24 hours after reading in the CRF. The entry of the local endoscopy is critical to initiate the blinded central reading process.

The mMS will be calculated using the SF and RB data from the daily eDiary (see the SoA, Section 1.3, and Section 8.1.2.3). The subscores of SF and RB will be calculated by averaging the daily subscores within the 7-day period, excluding the day of bowel preparation and day of endoscopy (for visits that include an endoscopy). The mMS cannot be calculated if the participant is not compliant with the daily eDiary entry of SF and RB data for a minimum of 3 consecutive days or 4 nonconsecutive days of the 7 days before bowel preparation for colonoscopy, or if no bowel preparation, then the day of the colonoscopy. For more details, refer to the SAP.

Scoring Each mMS subscore is scored on a 4-point scale, ranging from 0 to 3, to give a maximum mMS of 9. See Section 10.11 for more details about the mMS scoring system.

This study will use the mMS as outlined in the FDA Guidance (2016), which will include a sum of the following mMS subscores, with a maximum mMS of 9:

 SF  RB, and  ES.

8.1.1.2.

Endoscopy: Colonoscopy or Sigmoidoscopy Sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy will be used to determine the ES at screening and at other visits, as noted on the SoA. Lilly recommends that colonoscopy be used to document disease activity in all involved segments of the colon and that colonoscopy is preferred. The ES will be determined by  readings performed by qualified endoscopist who are blinded to induction treatment assignment, and  central readers who are blinded.

Note: Disagreement between the site reader and central reader will be adjudicated by an additional blinded central reader, as detailed in the Image Review charter.

Participants who are identified as being at increased risk for colon cancer or for adenomatous polyps or have not undergone recent surveillance for dysplasia will undergo a colonoscopy instead of a sigmoidoscopy to allow screening for dysplasia or to assess for the presence of adenomatous polyps, respectively.

A sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy will be performed on all participants during screening within 21 days prior to randomization and at other visits as specified in the SoA (Section 1.3). The sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy report and histopathology report must be available in the source documents. Prior to performing the screening sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy, investigators or designees should ensure that participants have clinically acceptable central laboratory test results, including stool tests that are “negative” for C. difficile and other intestinal pathogens (see Section 5).

91 If a participant undergoes early permanent discontinuation from the study soon after the screening sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy, there will be no need for EDV sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy. There is no need for an EDV sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy if fewer than 12 weeks have elapsed since a prior colonoscopy.

The endoscopist will be a licensed physician, who is qualified by education, training, and experience to perform sigmoidoscopies and colonoscopies. Investigators may delegate sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy to other authorized site personnel. However, authorized site personnel performing the sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy must receive training from the sponsor or designee in the determination and calculation of the ES. The endoscopist will determine the site-read ES at each sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy, and site personnel or their designee will record this in the CRF.

All sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy procedures will be video recorded in color using a storage medium provided by the sponsor or designee. The video images will be sent for independent central reading. The central imaging vendor will provide a manual that will outline the standard study procedures used to capture and transmit video recordings of endoscopic procedures throughout the study and will outline the qualifications required of the central reader. Recorded sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy procedures (without participant-identifying information) will be used for research purposes.

The central reader will determine the centrally read ES at each sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy in a blinded manner, as detailed in the Image Review charter.

The adjudicated ES will be provided to the site personnel prior to randomization to enable the determination of participant eligibility. An endoscopic score, as determined by the Image Review charter, will be used for endpoint determination and clinical responder status.

Lilly may partner with a vendor to use an AI-based continuous scoring system that quantifies the severity and extent of inflammation on endoscopy from endoscopic video recordings in addition to the original central reading of endoscopy.

If a participant becomes pregnant during the study, no additional sigmoidoscopies or colonoscopies will be performed.

Mitigating potential risks of colonoscopy See Sections 2.3.1 and 10.15.

8.1.2.

Secondary Efficacy Assessments Several secondary efficacy endpoints are based on  scores using the mMS described in Section 8.1.1.1  scores from the Geboes score for the assessment of histological activity, or  patient-reported outcome instruments.

8.1.2.1.

Colonic Biopsies A histopathology report supporting the diagnosis of UC must be available in the source documents prior to randomization to satisfy study entry criteria.

92 Biopsies will be obtained at each sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy to support assessment of the histopathology endpoints in this study and for further research purposes (without participant- identifying information), including the assessment of exploratory biomarkers. These will be sent to the central study laboratory for processing. Histopathologic scoring of these biopsies will be performed by a blinded central reader. The central imaging vendor will provide a manual that will outline the procedures to be used for secure specimen transfer, processing, slide preparation, and digitization of slides for histopathologic scoring. The histopathology results will not be made available to study sites. Investigators should obtain additional biopsies that are sent to the local laboratory for medical management of the participant.

8.1.2.2.

Geboes Score The Geboes Histological Index is based on a comprehensive grading system that evaluates aspects of mucosal injury seen in UC. The Geboes index has these grades:

 Grade 0 - Structural (architectural change)  Grade 1 - Chronic inflammatory infiltrate  Grade 2A - Lamina propria eosinophils  Grade 2B - Lamina propria neutrophils  Grade 3 - Neutrophils in epithelium  Grade 4 - Crypt destruction  Grade 5 - Erosion or ulceration For each of the histological features assessed, the highest grade in which there is evidence of disease is assigned (Geboes et al. 2000). The Geboes scale is further described in Section 10.12.

8.1.2.3.

Patient-Reported Outcomes: Daily Electronic Diary As stated in the SoA (Section 1.3), the participant’s daily electronic diary will include the following items, to rate their UC symptom severity and perception of disease severity:

Daily electronic diary item Description Rectal Bleeding (RB) See Section 8.1.1.1.

Stool Frequency (SF) See Section 8.1.1.1.

Patient Global Rating of Severity (PGR-S) The PGR-S is a patient-reported, single-item questionnaire to assess the UC symptom severity in participants over the past 24 hours. Responses are graded on a 6-point scale in which a score of one indicates the participant has no symptoms (that is, “none”) and a score of six indicates that the participant’s symptom(s) are “very severe.” Urgency NRS The Urgency NRS is a patient-reported, single-item instrument that measures the severity for the urgency, sudden, or immediate need, to have a bowel movement in the past 24 hours using an 11-point NRS ranging from 0 “no urgency” to 10 “worst possible urgency” (Dubinsky et al. 2022).

For eDiary compliance requirements, see Section 8.1.1.1.

8.1.2.4.

Patient-Reported Outcomes: Other Work Productivity and Activity Impairment Questionnaire: Ulcerative Colitis (WPAI:UC) 93 The WPAI:UC is a patient-reported instrument that measures the impact on work productivity and regular activities attributable to UC. It contains 6 items that assess  employment status  hours missed from work due to the specific health problem (UC)  hours missed from work for other reasons  hours actually worked  degree health affected productivity while working, and  degree health affected productivity in regular unpaid activities.

Four scores are calculated from the responses to these 6 items:

 absenteeism  presenteeism  work productivity loss, and  activity impairment.

Scores are calculated as impairment percentages (Reilly et al. 1993, 2008), with higher numbers indicating greater impairment and less productivity; that is, worse outcomes.

Inflammatory Bowel Disease Questionnaire (IBDQ) The IBDQ is a patient-reported, 32-item instrument that measures 4 aspects of the participants’ lives (Guyatt et al. 1989; Irvine et al. 1994, 1996, 1999):

 symptoms directly related to the primary bowel disturbance  systemic symptoms  emotional function, and  social function.

Responses are graded on a 7-point Likert scale, in which 7 denotes “not a problem at all” and 1 denotes “a very severe problem.” Scores range from 32 to 224. A higher score indicates a better quality of life (Irvine et al. 1994, 1999).

EQ-5D-5L The EQ-5D-5L (EuroQol Research Foundation 2019) is a standardized 5-item, self-administered instrument for use as a measure of health outcome. It provides a simple descriptive profile and a single index value for health status that can be used in the clinical and economic evaluation of health care as well as population health surveys. The EQ-5D-5L assesses 5 dimensions of health:

 mobility  self-care  usual activities  pain/discomfort, and  anxiety/depression.

Each dimension has 5 response levels:

 no problems  slight problems 94  moderate problems  severe problems, and  extreme problems.

The VAS records the respondent’s self-rated health on a vertical VAS where the endpoints are labeled as “The best health you can imagine” (100) and “The worst health you can imagine” (0).

8.1.2.5.

Extraintestinal Manifestations Review of EIMs will be performed as described in Section 8.2.1.

8.1.2.6.

Inflammatory Biomarkers CRP (high-sensitivity [hsCRP]) is an acute-phase protein expressed by hepatocytes in response to inflammatory cytokines, particularly IL-6, TNF, and IL-1β (Sands 2015).

Fecal calprotectin is a complex consisting of the calcium-binding proteins S100A8 and S100A9 (Sands 2015). It is expressed by activated neutrophils (and to a lesser extent by macrophages and monocytes), and fecal levels correlate with the number of neutrophils in the gut. It is used as a biomarker of intestinal inflammation in clinical practice.

8.1.3.

Exploratory Efficacy Assessment 8.1.3.1.

Assessment of Change in Body Fat Mass using Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) Total body composition assessments for this study It is recommended that study participants undergo a body composition assessment via DXA scans after meeting all eligibility criteria, including colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy, measured between Visits 1 and 2 and no later than Visit 3 prior to receiving study intervention and at Week 52 (Visit 15), or at the time of ED (if at least 3 months from the previous DXA scan), with the intent of evaluating changes in body composition associated with weight reduction, including both fat and lean mass compartments and abdominal visceral fat.

Recommendations for DXA body composition scans include the following:

 All scans for a given participant should be performed on the same DXA scanner using the same software.

 All scans for a given participant should be obtained under similar circumstances (e.g., similar time of day, consistent hydration status, and consistent scan status).

DXA scan DXA total body composition with regional analysis provides a measure of physiological response to obesity interventions superior to simple anthropometrics, such as BMI. It is safe and widely available in clinical practice (Kendler et al. 2013), making it a useful method to detect changes in fat and lean body mass in weight management studies.

The risk associated with DXA scan is low, with a radiation exposure (effective dose) of about 5 µSv or 0.005 mSv (millisievert). The typical level of background radiation to which the general population is exposed, not including radiation due to medical procedures, has been estimated to be about 2.5 mSv/year (Lewiecki et al. 2016).

95 DXA instrument Investigative sites will perform the body composition DXA scans on either Hologic® or Lunar™ DXA scanners with total body composition capabilities according to the imaging guidelines.

Guidance for conducting DXA scans To obtain consistent and acceptable quality data, investigators will receive detailed instructions on the DXA scan protocol to be used.

The scans will be read and evaluated by a central reader.

Recommendations Participants should fast for at least 8 hours without eating or drinking (except water) before each DXA scan. No water should be consumed within 2 hours before each DXA scan.

 Participants will abstain from strenuous exercise for 24 hours before each DXA scan.

 Perform all scans for a given participant using the same DXA scanner and software.

 Perform all scans for a given participant under similar circumstances, for example, using consistent scan status and performing the scan at the same time of day.

DXA scan contraindications Participants are excluded from the DXA scan if any of the following criteria apply but the participant may still enroll in Study AMCD:

 Have had a recent procedure (within 10 days) where oral contrast or radionuclides were administered (for example, CT scan with contrast or nuclear medicine studies).

 Have any implants, hardware, devices, or other foreign materials in the measurement area that may interfere with the scan, according to the DXA manufacturer’s specification.

 Have a body weight, height, and/or width that prohibits the ability to obtain accurate measurements according to the DXA manufacturer’s specification.

In these cases, missing DXA data will not be considered a protocol deviation.

data.name: Safety Assessments
data.text:
Planned time points for all safety assessments are provided in the SoA.

If safety monitoring uncovers GI AE-related issue that needs to be addressed by unblinding from tirzepatide treatment at the individual or treatment group level, additional analyses of the safety data can be performed by members of the external DMC (see Section 10.1.5.1).

8.2.1.

Physical Examinations Physical examinations will be performed when specified in the SoA (Section 1.3). Physical examinations may also be performed as clinically indicated at other visits at the discretion of the investigator.

96 Complete physical examination A complete physical examination will include, at a minimum,  general appearance  head, ears, eyes, nose, throat  extremities  assessments of the skin  assessment of lymph nodes  cardiovascular examination  respiratory examination  abdominal examination  neurological systems examination, and  thyroid examination.

Pelvic, rectal, and breast examinations are not required unless clinically indicated.

The screening physical examination should include the lifetime risk factors for TB infection, TB progression, and symptoms and/or signs of active TB, including measurement of body temperature and assessment of peripheral lymph nodes (Section 8.2.10).

Investigators should pay special attention to clinical signs related to previous serious illnesses.

Height and weight will also be measured and recorded per Section 10.9.

Symptom-directed physical assessments after screening These examinations are performed based on participant status and standard of care by a physician or other qualified healthcare professional.

Every symptom-directed examination should also include an examination of the heart, lungs, abdomen, neurological system, thyroid, and visual examination of the skin.

Every third month after screening, the physical examination should also include an assessment of TB risk factors and symptoms or signs of TB, including an assessment of peripheral lymph nodes (Section 8.2.10).

Extraintestinal manifestations EIMs will be reviewed at the time points described in the SoA (Section 1.3).

EIMs include  ankylosing spondylitis  osteoporosis  aphthous stomatitis  pancreatitis  arthralgia  peripheral arthritis  autoimmune hepatitis  primary sclerosing cholangitis  cholelithiasis  pyoderma gangrenosum  deep vein thrombosis  nephrolithiasis  episcleritis  sacroiliitis  erythema nodosum  skin vasculitis, and 97  iritis  uveitis  osteopenia 8.2.2.

Vital Signs For each participant, vital signs should be measured according to the SoA (Section 1.3) and Section 10.9. If warranted, additional vital signs may be measured.

Vital signs, including pulse (beats per minute) and blood pressure (mm Hg), will be measured after participant has been sitting for at least 5 minutes and before obtaining an ECG tracing and before collection of blood samples for laboratory testing, at visits where required.

Any clinically significant findings from vital-signs measurement that result in a diagnosis and that occur after the participant receives the first dose of study treatment should be reported to sponsor or its designee as an AE via the CRF.

8.2.3.

Electrocardiograms A 12-lead ECG (local) will be obtained as outlined in the SoA (Section 1.3) using an ECG machine that, preferably, automatically calculates the heart rate and measures PR, QRS, QT, and QTc intervals. The participant should be supine for at least 5 minutes before ECG collection, and remain supine but awake during ECG collection. ECGs should be collected prior to collection of blood samples for laboratory testing.

The ECGs must be interpreted by the investigator or qualified designee at the site as soon after the time of ECG collection as possible, and ideally while the participant is still present, for immediate participant management, if needed. The investigator or designee must document their review of the ECG. If a clinically relevant abnormality is observed on the participant’s ECG, then the investigator should assess the participant for symptoms, such as palpitations, near syncope, syncope, or chest pain.

The original ECG must be retained at the investigative site.

8.2.4.

Chest Imaging A high-quality, locally performed chest x-ray (posterior-anterior view and, if needed, a lateral view), interpreted and reported by a radiologist or pulmonologist, will be obtained as specified in the SoA (Section 1.3) for those with a positive TB test (Section 8.2.10).

For participants requiring chest imaging, the chest x-ray films, images, or a radiology report must be available to the investigator for review before the participant is randomly assigned to a treatment in this study.

Conditions for using a previous chest x-ray at screening Participants do not need to have a chest x-ray at screening if, in the opinion of the investigator, both of these 2 conditions are met:

 the chest x-ray was performed within 6 months before the initial screening, and  documentation of the prior chest x-ray, read by a qualified radiologist or pulmonologist, is sufficient for TB evaluation according to local standard of care.

98 Alternatives to chest x-ray In consultation with the sponsor’s medical monitor, results of a chest CT scan or other imaging study similar to a chest x-ray, if performed within the same time window, may be used instead of a chest x-ray for the TB evaluation.

8.2.5.

Clinical Safety Laboratory Tests See Section 10.2 for the list of clinical laboratory tests to be performed and the SoA for the timing and frequency.

Reviewing and recording test results The investigator must review the laboratory results, document this review, and report any clinically relevant changes occurring during the study as an AE. The laboratory results must be retained with source documents unless a Source Document Agreement or comparable document cites an electronic location that accommodates the expected retention duration. Clinically significant abnormal laboratory findings are those which are not associated with the underlying disease, unless judged by the investigator to be more severe than expected for the participant's condition.

Repeat testing after clinically significant abnormal findings All laboratory tests with values considered clinically significantly abnormal during participation in the study should be repeated until the values return to normal or baseline or are no longer considered clinically significant by the investigator or medical monitor. For details about managing hepatic laboratory abnormalities, see Section 8.2.9.

If such values do not return to normal/baseline within a period of time judged reasonable by the investigator, the etiology should be identified and the sponsor notified.

All protocol-required laboratory assessments, as defined in Section 10.2, must be conducted in accordance with the SoA, standard collection requirements, and laboratory manual.

If laboratory values from non-protocol specified laboratory assessments performed at an investigator-designated local laboratory require a change in participant management or are considered clinically significant by the investigator, for example, SAE or AE or dose modification, then report the information as an AE.

8.2.6.

Pregnancy Testing Pregnancy testing is to be performed for all IOCBP and will occur as outlined in the SoA (Section 1.3).

Serum and urine pregnancy tests must be performed only for IOCBP, prior to administering study intervention or must be performed with the result available prior to first dose or injection of study intervention(s).

99 Additional pregnancy tests (beyond those required per the SoA) should be performed at any time during the study  if a menstrual period is missed  if there is clinical suspicion of pregnancy, or  as required by local law or regulation.

If the participant is pregnant, the participant must be permanently discontinued from study intervention and be withdrawn from the study (Section 7.2).

Assessment of FSH levels can assist in determining if an individual AFAB meets the definition of “menopausal” as outlined in Section 10.4.1. FSH levels can be optimally obtained at screening or during the study, at the discretion of the investigator to determine menopausal status (Section 1.3).

8.2.7.

Suicidal Ideation and Behavior Risk Monitoring Baseline assessment of suicidal ideation and behavior (SIB) and intervention-emergent SIB will be monitored using the C-SSRS. See Section 8.3.3.7 for more details.

Participants should be monitored appropriately and observed closely for SIB or any other unusual changes in behavior throughout the study.

Participants who experience signs of SIB should undergo a risk assessment. All factors contributing to SIB should be evaluated and consideration should be given to discontinuation of the study intervention (Section 7.1.1).

Family and caregivers of participants should be alerted about the need to monitor participants for the emergence of unusual changes in behavior, as well as the emergence of SIB and to report such symptoms immediately to the study investigator.

8.2.8.

Depression Monitoring Depression will be monitored using the QIDS-SR16 (Section 8.3.3.8) and appropriate actions will be taken (Section 8.3.3.8), including potential discontinuation of study intervention (Section 7.1.1).

Study site personnel should monitor participants receiving study intervention for depression or any other unusual changes in behavior throughout the study.

Close Hepatic Monitoring If a participant develops any one of these changes, initiate close hepatic monitoring.

Close hepatic monitoring should include these actions:

 Laboratory tests((Section 10.5), including ALT, AST, ALP, TBL, D. Bil, GGT, CK, and CBC with differential, should be checked within 48 to 72 hours of the detection of elevated liver tests to confirm the abnormality and to determine if it is increasing or decreasing.

 If the abnormality persists, clinical and laboratory monitoring should continue at a frequency of 2 to 3 times weekly until levels start normalizing or return to approximate baseline values. Subsequently, the frequency of monitoring may be lowered to once every 1 to 2 weeks if the participant’s clinical condition and lab results stabilize.

 In addition to lab tests, basic evaluation for possible causes of abnormal liver tests should be initiated by the investigator in consultation with the Lilly-designated medical monitor.

At a minimum, this evaluation should include physical examination and a thorough medical history, including current symptoms, recent illnesses (for example, heart failure, systemic infection, hypotension, or seizures), recent travel, concomitant medications (including over-the-counter), herbal and dietary supplements, history of alcohol drinking and other substance abuse.

 Clinical and laboratory monitoring should continue at a frequency of 2 to 3 times weekly until levels start normalizing or return to approximate baseline values.

 At a minimum, comprehensive hepatic evaluation should include physical examination and a thorough medical history, as outlined above, as well as tests for PT-INR; tests for viral hepatitis A, B, C, and E; tests for autoimmune hepatitis; and an abdominal imaging study (for example, ultrasound or CT scan). Remaining samples collected for hepatic evaluation may be stored as an exploratory biomarker samples. These stored samples will be used for the limited purpose of additional hepatic evaluations for up to 15 years.

 Based on the participant’s history and initial results, further testing should be considered in consultation with the Lilly-designated medical monitor, including tests for hepatitis D virus, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, acetaminophen levels, acetaminophen protein adducts, urine toxicology screen, Wilson’s disease, blood alcohol levels, urinary ethyl glucuronide, and blood phosphatidylethanol (PEth).

 For participants with isolated ALP elevation ≥2.5x ULN without GGT elevation, consider testing for ALP isoenzymes and evaluating for extrahepatic sources, such as bone disease (e.g., fractures, bone metastases, osteomalacia, Paget’s disease), or pregnancy.

 Based on the circumstances and the investigator’s assessment of the participant’s clinical condition, the investigator should consider referring the participant for a hepatologist or gastroenterologist consultation and additional tests, including magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatograph, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatograph, cardiac echocardiogram, or a liver biopsy.

 All the medical information and test results related to the hepatic monitoring and comprehensive hepatic evaluation should be collected and recorded in CRFs, including the hepatic safety CRF.

Interruption or discontinuation of study drug should include these actions:

 While the participant is not receiving the study drug, clinical and laboratory monitoring should continue at a frequency of 1 to 3 times weekly until liver tests normalize or return to approximate baseline values.

 If the hepatic event continues past the anticipated end of the study (that is, data lock) the investigator should consult with the sponsor-designated medical monitor to determine the need for further data collection beyond the end date of the study (that is, data lock date).

 All the medical information and tests results related to the close hepatic monitoring and comprehensive hepatic evaluation should be collected and recorded in a hepatic safety CRF.

 Resumption of the study drug after interruption for a hepatic reason can be considered only in consultation with the sponsor designated medical monitor and only if the liver test results returned to near baseline and if a self-limited non-study-drug etiology is identified.

 Otherwise, both study drugs should be permanently discontinued.

104 8.2.10.

Tuberculosis Testing and Monitoring Screening During screening, all participants are to be assessed for risk factors, symptoms, and signs of TB with all of the following:

 thorough history to determine the lifetime risk factors for TB infection, for TB progression, and for symptoms and/or signs of active TB, and  signs of previous or active TB by means of o thorough physical examination for signs of active TB, including measurement of body temperature (Section 8.2.2) and assessment of peripheral lymph nodes (Section 8.2.1), and o a high-quality chest x-ray (posterior-anterior view, including a lateral view if needed) or if a participant has a positive TB test, interpreted and reported by a radiologist or pulmonologist (Section 8.2.4).

All participants with no history of LTBI or active TB, and no history of positive Mantoux TST using PPD or positive M. tuberculosis IGRA must have one of the following tests:

 PPD TST, or  IGRA for M. tuberculosis.

Retesting One retest is allowed for participants with an “indeterminate” QuantiFERON-TB Gold assay or “borderline” T-SPOT.TB assay. Participants with 2 indeterminate QuantiFERON-TB Gold assays or 2 borderline T-SPOT.TB assays will be excluded (Section 5.4.1).

Diagnosed LTBI Participants diagnosed with LTBI are excluded (Section 5.2) unless they are candidates for LTBI treatment, are being treated for LTBI, and the following criteria are met:

 After receiving at least 4 weeks of appropriate LTBI therapy (as per the WHO or US CDC guidelines), there is no evidence of hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST must remain ≤2 times ULN) or other treatment intolerance. In this case, the participant may be rescreened (Section 5.4.2) and is not excluded due to LTBI.

 The participant must continue and complete appropriate LTBI therapy to remain eligible to continue receiving study intervention (Section 7.1).

Monitoring during the study For all participants, monitoring for TB is to be continuous throughout the study. At a minimum, each participant is to have the following documented at least every 3 months:

 thorough history to determine any risk factors for TB infection and for TB progression, and symptoms or signs of active TB, and  thorough physical examination for signs of active TB, including measurement of body temperature and assessment of peripheral lymph nodes (Sections 8.2.2 and 8.2.1).

105 8.2.11.

Hepatitis B Testing and Monitoring As specified in the SoA (Section 1.3), initial testing for HBV infection includes HBsAg and anti-HBc.

 If HBsAg is positive, the participant is excluded.

 If HBsAg is negative and anti-HBc is negative, the participant is not excluded.

 If HBsAg is negative and anti-HBc is positive, further testing for HBV DNA is required.

○ If the screening HBV DNA is positive, the participant is excluded.

○ If the screening HBV DNA is negative, the participant is not excluded. Repeat testing for HBV DNA is required at least every 3 months during the study.

Management of participants with treatment-emergent detectable HBV DNA during the study Follow the guidance in these tables:

Management of participants with previously undetectable HBV DNA If … Then… a participant with previously undetectable HBV DNA has treatment-emergent detectable but not quantifiable HBV DNA  Withhold mirikizumab.

 Repeat HBV DNA, HBsAg, ALT, AST, TBL within 2 weeks and again 2 weeks later.

 If the repeat HBV DNA is undetectable or detectable but not quantifiable on 2 consecutive tests, and the participant remains asymptomatica with no elevation in liver testsb, resume mirikizumab with close monitoring of HBV DNA and liver tests.

 Wait for the results of both HBV DNA tests before making a decision on resuming mirikizumab.

 Monitor HBV DNA, ALT, AST, TBL at least once monthly in the first 3 months after the detectable HBV DNA result and every 2-3 months thereafter.

 If one of the subsequent HBV DNA results again becomes detectable and not quantifiable, but the participant remains asymptomatic with normal liver tests, continue mirikizumab, and increase monitoring frequency of HBV DNA, ALT, AST, TBL to once monthly.

 If one of the repeat HBV DNA results is detectable and quantifiable, follow the instructions below, for participants with 106 Management of participants with previously undetectable HBV DNA treatment-emergent detectable and quantifiable HBV DNA.

a participant with previously undetectable HBV DNA has treatment-emergent detectable and quantifiable HBV DNA:

 If the participant is asymptomatica and liver tests are not elevatedb:

 Withhold mirikizumab.

 Repeat HBV DNA, HBsAg, ALT, AST, TBL within 2 weeks.

 Inform the sponsor designated medical monitor.

 Refer to a hepatologistc for further management including initiation of a nucleoside/nucleotide analog (NA).

 Continue monitoring HBV DNA, HBsAg, ALT, AST, TBL every 2 weeks. If HBV DNA remains undetectable in 3 consecutive tests, and liver tests are not elevatedb, monitoring frequency can decrease to once every 1-2 months.

 If NA was initiated, and HBV DNA remains undetectable in 3 consecutive tests, monitoring frequency can be decreased to once every 2-3 months.

 If the participant is symptomatica, or if ALT, AST, or TBL are elevatedb:

 Withhold mirikizumab.

 Repeat HBsAg, ALT, AST, TBL within 48-72 hours to determine if the levels are increasing or decreasing.

 Continue monitoring liver tests 1-3 times weekly according to the protocol requirements for treatment-emergent abnormal liver tests.

 Inform the sponsor-designated medical monitor.

 Refer to a hepatologistc for further management including initiation of a nucleoside/ nucleotide analog (NA).

 Continue monitoring HBV DNA, HBsAg, every 2 weeks. If liver tests are back to baseline, and HBV DNA remains undetectable in 3 consecutive tests, monitoring frequency can decrease to once monthly.

 If NA was initiated, liver tests are back to baseline, and HBV DNA remains undetectable in 3 consecutive tests, monitoring frequency can be decreased to once every 2-3 months.

 If NA was initiated and mirikizumab was resumed, monitor HBV DNA, HBsAg, ALT, AST, TBL at least monthly.

 If NA was initiated and mirikizumab was resumed, NA treatment and HBV DNA monitoring should continue for at least 6 months after discontinuation of mirikizumab.

Note: After completion of the study monitoring, refer the participant to a hepatologistc for continued follow-up and management.

 HBV DNA is detectable and quantifiable with concurrent symptomsa that are considered by the investigator to be related to HBV reactivation.

 HBV DNA viral load is >100 IU/mL on 2 or more tests.

Permanently discontinue mirikizumab.

a Symptoms may include worsening fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, jaundice, fever, or rash.

b ALT, AST, or TBL elevation refers to elevations ≥2x ULN in participants with normal baseline or near normal baseline (that is, <1.5x ULN) or elevation ≥2x baseline in participants with elevated baseline (that is, ≥1.5x ULN). . In participants with Gilbert’s syndrome, the threshold for TBL will be TBL ≥3x ULN, if baseline is <1.5x ULN, and TBL ≥2x baseline, if baseline is ≥1.5x ULN.

c A hepatologist may include a health care provider with recognized expertise in the assessment and management of viral hepatitis.

8.2.12.

Hepatitis C Testing As specified in the SoA (Section 1.3), initial testing for HCV infection includes testing for anti-HCV.

 If anti-HCV is positive, a test for circulating HCV RNA is required.

 If HCV RNA test is negative, the participant is not excluded.

 If HCV RNA test is positive, the participant is excluded (see Section 5.2).

Participants who have had HCV infection and have been successfully treated, defined as a sustained virologic response (HCV RNA by PCR negative for at least 24 weeks following treatment completion), are not excluded on the basis of HCV as long as HCV RNA test is negative at screening.

If HCV RNA is detected during the study, the study intervention will be discontinued (Section 7.1.1), and the participant should receive appropriate follow-up medical care.

8.2.13.

Malnutrition Malnutrition is a term broadly used to describe deficiencies or excesses in the intake of macronutrients, micronutrients, or energy, as well as the physiological changes that can result.

109 As stated in Section 5.3.3, medical staff should monitor participants for signs and symptoms of malnutrition. A table of signs and symptoms associated with common nutrient deficiencies is included in Section 10.7. The nutritional panel described in Section 10.2.2 should be collected if  the PI suspects the participant may have malnutrition, for example, caloric intake is significantly reduced to below 800 to 1200 kcal  a participant’s BMI falls below 22 kg/m2, or  in participants with T2DM, weight loss is >20% or >4 kg/month.

A clinical assessment of dietary intake and nutritional status should also be completed.

Nutritional guidance and, as needed, supplementation, should be considered. For severe or persistent cases, consider discontinuation of tirzepatide (Section 7.1.1), and discuss management of the participant with the medical monitor. The treatment of deficiencies should be managed in line with local clinical guidelines. If additional guidance is required, reach out to the sponsor- designated medical monitor.

8.2.14.

Gallbladder Disease and Tirzepatide Gallbladder problems including gallstones have been reported uncommonly in patients taking tirzepatide and GLP-1 receptor agonists. In the tirzepatide SURMOUNT trials, cholelithiasis was reported in 1.1%, cholecystitis was reported in 0.7%, and cholecystectomy was reported in 0.2% of tirzepatide-treated patients. Risk may be increased if patients have diabetes or obesity and in cases of rapid weight loss. Some gallbladder problems may need surgery. To minimize the risk of gallbladder problems, investigators should aim for gradual weight loss of 1 to 2 pounds per week from tirzepatide in participants, monitor participants for signs of gallbladder disease (such as severe upper abdominal pain), and advise participants to avoid a very high-fat diet, fried or greasy foods.

data.text:
The definitions of the following events can be found in Section 10.3:

 AEs  SAEs, and  product complaints.

These events will be reported by the participant, or, when appropriate, by a caregiver or surrogate.

The investigator and any qualified designees are responsible for detecting, documenting, and recording events that meet these definitions and remain responsible for following up events that are serious, considered related to the study intervention or study procedures, or that caused the participant to discontinue the study (see Section 7).

Care will be taken not to introduce bias when detecting events. Open-ended and non-leading verbal questioning of the participant is the preferred method to inquire about event occurrences.

After the initial report, the investigator is required to proactively follow each participant at subsequent visits or contacts. All SAEs and AEs of special interest (as defined in Section 8.3.3) 110 will be followed until resolution, stabilization, the event is otherwise explained, or the participant is lost to follow-up (as defined in Section 7.3).

For product complaints, the investigator is responsible for ensuring that follow-up includes any supplemental investigations as indicated to elucidate the nature or causality. Further information on follow-up procedures is provided in Section 10.3.
